rationale: HeyCharge sells EV charging hardware and platform software to utilities, property operators, and mobility providers. The closest fit is Energy, which covers power distribution and energy management products sold to utilities and industrial customers. Automotive is the main alternative, but that category is about vehicles and their supporting systems, whereas this is charging infrastructure.

Mecho is an on-demand marketplace that matches vehicle owners and businesses with vetted mechanics and spare part vendors. It sells car maintenance and repair services to individuals, which fits "vehicle ownership management" under Transportation Services in the Consumer domain. The other candidate was Home and Personal, but the vehicle focus makes Transportation Services the better match.

Wibond is a buy-now-pay-later product. It gives underbanked consumers installment credit at the checkout of online merchants, so the core of what it sells is credit. Fintech → Credit and Lending fits better than Payments, even though it is integrated into the purchase flow.

Hundred sells automated visual inspection systems to factories, which are industrial automation customers. The best fit is Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics. The company's main focus is manufacturing quality control rather than consumer electronics sold to consumers.

Flint sells an AI learning platform to K-12 schools and districts, so education is the sector that fits. The fund's definitions list education under "Other", and none of the B2B subindustries is specifically about education.

Rethoric sells LinkedIn content strategy, writing and scheduling to companies and founders, so they stay visible to their target customers. That is a marketing function (engaging customers through content), so B2B Marketing fits best.

Green Canopy NODE makes flat-pack house assembly kits in its own factory and builds with them as a developer and general contractor. Its prefab components and software go to contractors and into its own residential projects, so I'm placing it in Real Estate and Construction. Within that domain, Construction fits better than Housing and Real Estate, because the core offering is technology and components for building structures rather than a marketplace for already-built properties.

Peakflo sells software to finance teams that automates invoice-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and expense reimbursement. That is accounts payable and receivable work, so it fits B2B Finance and Accounting better than Operations, even though the pitch mentions back-office operations.

Junction Bioscience builds an AI platform for molecular discovery and uses it to develop its own therapies in neuroinflammation and immunology. The description reads as drug discovery, although it also talks about developing therapies for patients. The product at the center of the pitch is the AI hypothesis engine, a computational research platform. That fits Drug Discovery and Delivery better than Therapeutics.

Polar gives freelancers and remote workers outside the U.S. a USD account in their name and lets them convert and withdraw earnings through local bank transfers or stablecoins. The core offering is holding dollar balances and exchanging currency, so Banking and Exchange fits better than Payments, which focuses on per-transaction processing. It could also be read as Consumer Finance, since its users are individuals, but account holding and currency conversion is the main product.
Swadesi Way is an organic food brand that sells to individual consumers, so it fits Consumer, Food and Beverage.

Belvo sells an open finance API to companies and developers, much like Plaid does in the US. It sits between banks and the fintech apps built on top of them, so I placed it in Fintech. Of the Fintech subindustries, Banking and Exchange fits best because it covers core banking and compliance software sold to financial institutions. Payments is a weaker fit because Belvo mainly provides access to financial data rather than moving money.
Albacore builds drone submarines for military operators, which fits Defense. The "Drones" subindustry covers unmanned aerial vehicles, and this product is underwater and sold for warfare.

Educato sells exam-prep content directly to students, which is education. The fund's Other domain covers education, and its Consumer subindustries (such as Job and Career Services) are about employment and career skills rather than academic exam prep, so I classified it under Other.

Pixley's main product is a consumer platform where families create personalized animated cartoons, which is content creation and consumption by kids. The B2B Pixley Studios service is secondary. Of the Consumer subindustries, Content fits best, since the core offering is produced animated media, not social interaction or gaming.

Yummy Future builds robots for restaurants and food retail businesses, which are business customers rather than individual consumers. Its closest fit is industrial automation, so I placed it under Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics. The B2B Retail subindustry was the other candidate, but that one is aimed at storefront and commerce software rather than robotic hardware.

Automax.ai is an appraisal firm that sells property valuations to lenders and others in real estate transactions. That points to Real Estate and Construction. Its appraisal reports serve the buying, selling and financing of already-built properties, and the company is not selling tools to construction firms. Housing and Real Estate is the better fit than Construction.

Hemlock sells a wrist-worn EMG hardware device and force data to robotics labs for training robot policies. The buyers are robotics and manufacturing automation customers, so Industrials → Manufacturing and Robotics fits better than the B2B or Healthcare categories.

Buoyant Aero builds autonomous drone blimps, which are unmanned aerial vehicles. They are sold to advertisers and brands as a physical advertising platform. The Drones subindustry fits best because the core product is the unmanned aircraft itself.

Candor sells AI software to defense and deeptech startups to find and apply for government funding opportunities. The closest fit is B2B Sales, because the product pursues revenue opportunities (government contracts and grants) on the customer's behalf. It is not an Industrials/Defense company, since it doesn't build defense technology itself.

CharacterQuilt sells AI agents to enterprise marketing teams that build and deploy campaigns in tools like HubSpot, Marketo and LinkedIn. That is software for businesses to run marketing campaigns, so it fits B2B, Marketing.
Creizer provides revenue-based financing to online sellers (SMEs) in LATAM, which is a lending product, so Fintech and Credit and Lending fit best.

UPchieve is an education nonprofit that gives free tutoring to low-income high school students. None of the product domains fit it, because it isn't selling to consumers or businesses, so I classified it under Other, which the fund defines to include education and nonprofits.

UrbanKisaan builds foundation models for plant genomics and phenotype prediction, along with controlled-environment chambers that speed up breeding cycles and grow crops commercially. Its customers are breeders, growers, and agribusinesses, so Industrials > Agriculture fits best. The definition names plant biology research tools and food production systems explicitly.

Skymerse sells AI software to airlines for flight operations, covering planning, monitoring and cockpit support. Its customers are businesses, and the product is operational software rather than aircraft, engines or space infrastructure. That points to Industrials, Aviation and Space as one option, but the "Aviation and Space" definition centres on selling spacecraft, satellites and aircraft engines or related infrastructure and data services. The B2B "Operations" subindustry fits software for internal workflows that don't fit another function. I'm choosing Aviation and Space because the product is built for airline flight operations, which is the industry's core domain.

Wren sells a monthly subscription to individual consumers so they can offset their carbon footprint. That fits the Climate subindustry of Industrials, which covers carbon reduction, removal, and emissions-accounting products. The alternative is a Consumer subindustry, but none of them cover carbon offsets, so Climate is the closest match.

PNOĒ sells a clinical-grade breath analysis device, with software and expert support, to health professionals and clinics. It measures metabolic function (VO2max) to assess a patient's health state and prescribe personalized programs. This is a physical diagnostic and measurement product, so the best fit is Healthcare, and Diagnostics is closer than Medical Devices or Consumer Health and Wellness. The device detects and characterizes metabolic and cardiopulmonary state, and the buyers are clinicians, not individual consumers.

Code Four sells AI software to police departments that automates report writing and transcription from body camera footage. The closest fit is B2B rather than Defense, because Defense covers weapons, protective equipment, and surveillance for combat applications, and this is administrative workflow software. Within B2B, the best match is Operations, which covers software for internal workflows that don't fit finance, HR, sales, or marketing.

Abalone Bio develops activating antibody drugs, starting with obesity and metabolic disease. It also has pharma partnerships and an in-house drug pipeline. Its core output is therapeutic drug candidates rather than a platform sold as a tool, so Therapeutics fits better than Drug Discovery and Delivery.

LineLeap's main product is a consumer mobile app for buying line-skip passes, drinks, cover, and event tickets at nightlife venues. That fits Consumer, in the Travel, Leisure and Tourism subindustry, which covers leisure experiences sold directly to individuals. Venues also use LineLeap's technology for marketing, so B2B was a possible fit. But the core offering and the million-plus customers it has acquired are consumers.

Star sells an AI tool that lets individuals make games without coding. The buyers appear to be individual creators and hobbyists rather than businesses, so it fits Consumer. Within Consumer, Gaming (games and game-adjacent entertainment products) is a closer fit than Virtual and Augmented Reality, since the product is about making and playing games, not immersive 3D simulation.
FitHub is an online supermarket that sells healthy groceries directly to consumers in Colombia, so Consumer / Food and Beverage fits best.

Fifth Door lets everyday consumers create, share, and play games with AI. That puts it in Consumer, and the best-fitting subindustry is Gaming, since the core offering is games and game creation rather than immersive VR/AR.

Soteri Skin sells skincare products directly to consumers, so Consumer fits better than Healthcare. Within Consumer, Apparel and Cosmetics covers beauty and personal care products, and the product is non-prescription, which makes Consumer Health and Wellness the closer alternative. The D2C skincare product is still a beauty and personal care good, so Apparel and Cosmetics is the best match.

Canix sells software to cannabis businesses to manage compliance and day-to-day operations across cultivation, processing, and distribution. That is B2B software, and the closest subindustry is Operations, since it covers internal workflows that don't fit finance, HR, sales, or marketing. Infrastructure also lists compliance automation, but that means technical building blocks other software runs on, which doesn't describe Canix's end-user operations product.

Pronto is a ride-sharing and delivery platform that sells mobility services to individual consumers in Latin American cities. That matches Consumer, Transportation Services, which covers ride-sharing. Its subscription model for drivers doesn't change that, since the core product is the ride service for riders.

Elevate offers USD deposit accounts, with ACH, wires and a debit card, to non-US residents. That is account holding rather than per-transaction payment processing, so Banking and Exchange fits better than Payments or Consumer Finance.

Bemlo sells AI scheduling and workforce management software to healthcare and social care organizations. That is software for managing their administrative and operational workflows, not a product that diagnoses, treats, or cares for patients directly, so Healthcare IT fits best.
Bild AI sells AI estimating and takeoff software to construction subcontractors and suppliers. It reads blueprints, builds door schedules, and prices bids, which fits the Construction subindustry.
Clupp's products are insurance policies, brokerage software, and insurance-backed financing guarantees, which fit the Fintech domain and its Insurance subindustry.

Chestnut is itself a mortgage lender that uses AI agents to originate loans for consumers (purchases, refinances, cash-outs). Because it sells loans directly, Fintech / Credit and Lending fits better than Housing and Real Estate.
Momento is building a licensed auto insurance carrier in Mexico that will underwrite risk and set prices for underserved drivers. That fits Fintech, and within it Insurance.

Proximitty sells AI software to banks and fintechs that automates commercial loan underwriting, financial spreading, loan operations and covenant tracking. Of the Fintech subindustries, Credit and Lending fits best because its definition covers lending infrastructure and automation sold to financial institutions.

Keylika develops a new small-molecule iron drug delivered through a skin patch, intended for regulatory approval to treat iron deficiency anemia. That makes it a company selling a finished therapeutic, so Healthcare / Therapeutics fits best.

Ten Lives optimizes microbial factories (precision fermentation) to produce proteins at low cost. This is biomanufacturing using engineered organisms, and the proteins are for sustainable protein sourcing rather than therapeutic use. That fits Healthcare / Industrial Bio, which covers engineered organisms and biomanufacturing processes sold to industrial customers for non-therapeutic uses.

TwentyTwo builds a defensive stack against engineered pandemics, which is a biosecurity use case. The fund has no biosecurity category, so I weighed three options.

- **Security (B2B):** this covers protecting systems, data, or communications, which is a poor match for biological threats.
- **Defense (Industrials):** this covers weapons, surveillance, and countermeasure technologies sold to government and security customers. Biodefense for national security fits this best.
- **Diagnostics (Healthcare):** this could fit if the product were biological threat detection, but the description centers on AI infrastructure and prevention rather than testing.

I chose Defense because the company sells a protective, countermeasure-style stack against bio threats, likely to government and security customers.

Tsenta sells directly to individual job seekers, using an AI agent to find matching jobs and apply on their behalf. That fits the Consumer domain, and within it the Job and Career Services subindustry.

Zeta Surgical sells FDA-cleared surgical navigation and robotics hardware and systems to clinicians. These physical systems interact with the patient's body to guide surgical and neuro-therapeutic procedures, so Medical Devices fits better than Healthcare IT.

Gauss sells consumers a product that refinances their debt, using a line of credit it originates to pay off expensive card balances. That is a credit product for individuals rather than broader financial planning, so Credit and Lending fits better than Consumer Finance.

Vitable Health sells ICHRA health benefits bundled with direct primary care (virtual visits, prescriptions, labs) to startups and SMBs. The care itself is delivered by clinicians, so Healthcare Services fits better than Healthcare IT or an HR benefits tool. Insurance is a weaker fit because the core offering is care delivery rather than risk underwriting.
Olio Labs develops its own combination drug candidates, with lead programs in obesity. It sells therapeutics rather than research platforms or tools, so Healthcare, Therapeutics is the best fit.

Astor sells an AI investment advisor to individual retail investors, which fits Fintech and, within it, Asset Management: investment decision-making and wealth advisory tools for individual investors.
Deploy sells deployment infrastructure for generalist robots to businesses that need them, which fits industrial automation and robotics best.

MaverickX sells chemical solutions to oil and mining operators to improve extraction of oil from shale and metals such as lithium from low-grade ores. Its customers are energy and mining companies, so Industrials fits. Within that domain, Energy is the closest subindustry because its core offerings serve oil production and the resource and lithium supply chain. Agriculture, Climate, and Manufacturing and Robotics fit worse.
HitPay sells payment acceptance and processing infrastructure (cards, QR, wallets, local rails) to businesses, which fits Fintech and the Payments subindustry.

Tranqui is a digital debt collection and repayment company, so I placed it in Fintech. Of the Fintech subindustries, Credit and Lending fits best, since debt collection and repayment plans sit within the credit lifecycle. Consumer Finance is the closest alternative, but it focuses on personal financial planning rather than credit and collections.

Lygg develops a new UVA-protective skincare ingredient. The ingredient would most likely be sold to sunscreen and skincare brands, but the company could also sell to consumers directly. The closest fit is the Consumer domain under Apparel and Cosmetics, which covers beauty and personal care products. The other candidates, such as Drug Discovery and Delivery or Industrial Bio, fit less well.

DeepAware sells robots and robot parts, plus data collection, reinforcement learning environments, and deployment services, to enterprises and researchers. That fits Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry, which covers industrial automation systems and robots sold to manufacturers and industrial operators.

Splash builds autonomous patrol boats for national security customers, and its stated aim is to replace traditional naval vessels. That makes Defense the best fit, since it covers surveillance and weapons technologies sold to military and government customers. Automotive covers ground transportation only, so it doesn't apply to boats.

Atlia sells short-term rental property management to property owners, so the buyer is an owner of already-built residential property who hands over operations and pays a management fee. That fits Housing and Real Estate, which covers services for landlords and owners to manage built properties. It does not fit Construction, and it is not a software tool sold to other businesses.

Chiron is an iPad app that checks handwritten math as students write it, which is a learning product aimed at individual consumers. None of the consumer subindustries is education, and the company isn't a fit for any other domain, so "Other" (which covers education) is the best match.

Nabla Bio sells AI-driven antibody design capabilities to pharmaceutical and biotech companies, working as a research and design platform partner rather than selling a finished therapeutic itself. That fits Drug Discovery and Delivery best.

CatchBack Cards sells a consumer app where collectors open digital mystery packs, buy and sell cards, and have physical cards shipped to them. The opening of mystery packs with custom odds is a form of gaming and wagering, so Gaming fits better than Apparel and Cosmetics, which covers wearables and beauty products.

The Token Company sells compression middleware that developers place in front of LLM calls to cut context bloat, lowering cost and latency. It is a technical building block that other software runs on top of, so Infrastructure fits better than Engineering, Product and Design, which is for tools used to build and ship products.

Klaimee sells liability insurance policies, plus risk evaluation and certification, to companies deploying AI agents. The Fintech Insurance subindustry covers companies that sell insurance policies, brokerage, or underwriting and risk-assessment technology to consumers or businesses, which matches this offering.

Ultrasonium sells a new metal manufacturing process, with a physical AI control layer, to aerospace, energy, and compute customers. That fits industrial automation and factory infrastructure sold to manufacturers, so I've classified it under Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics.

TovenAI sells AI agents to compliance teams at institutional trading firms. The closest fit is Fintech, since the customers are financial institutions. The alternatives were B2B Legal or Security, and Banking and Exchange, which covers "core banking and compliance software to financial institutions", is the best match among the Fintech subindustries.

Cardamon sells AI software to compliance teams at regulated financial firms. The closest fit is a B2B product rather than Fintech. The Legal subindustry covers compliance and in-house legal team workflows, and the product translates regulation into obligations and product requirements, which is that kind of work.

Vinci Games makes multiplayer VR games for individual players. The Consumer domain has both a Gaming subindustry and a Virtual and Augmented Reality one. The VR subindustry is defined by immersive 3D tooling and experiences, while Gaming is defined by gameplay itself. Since Vinci sells game titles (Blacktop Hoops, Ruffnauts) and the value is the gameplay, Gaming fits best, even though the games run on VR hardware.

Ontra sells software to transit agencies and cities to optimize transit planning and operations. The Industrials Automotive subindustry covers supporting software for ground transportation of people sold to transit agencies, which fits best.

PrimeVault sells digital asset and stablecoin infrastructure (wallets, treasury, compliance, market access) to enterprises and financial institutions. That fits Fintech, and within it Banking and Exchange, which covers crypto trading infrastructure and core banking and compliance software sold to financial institutions. Payments was the closest alternative, but the product is centered on custody, issuance, and market access rather than per-transaction processing.

Baraka is a retail investment app that lets individual investors in the Middle East buy stocks and ETFs. That puts it in Fintech, and Asset Management fits better than Banking and Exchange because the product centers on investing and portfolio building for individuals.

Breezeful is an online mortgage broker that sells mortgage origination and brokering to individual borrowers. That is closest to Credit and Lending, which covers loans and lending services for individuals.

OlaClick sells software to restaurants (digital menus, WhatsApp ordering, POS, CRM/marketing). That matches the B2B Retail subindustry, which covers software sold to retail, restaurant, or merchant businesses for managing storefronts and consumer-facing commerce.

FrontPage's core offering is a community where traders and investors connect, share ideas, and learn from each other. That is interpersonal connection rather than consumption of produced media, so the Consumer domain's Social subindustry fits better than Content or the Fintech options.

Tokenless sells tools and research to teams that train models with RL, build environments, or run agent evals. Its products help them find and fix flaws in those environments. That makes it a tool for AI and ML builders, so I'm placing it under B2B, in Engineering, Product and Design, rather than Infrastructure or Analytics.

Kingdom develops microbe-derived ingredients (Superculture®) for pet and human health and sells them as ingredients, which points to a B2B model, with pet and consumer health and wellness brands as the likely buyers. The closest fits in the fund's categories are:

- **Consumer Health and Wellness** sells directly to consumers, which doesn't match an ingredients supplier.
- **Industrial Bio** covers engineered organisms and bio-based materials for non-therapeutic industrial uses. Kingdom's microbial ingredients are natural microbes, and they are used in health products rather than industrial processes.
- **Drug Discovery and Delivery** is aimed at biotech and pharma, which isn't Kingdom's market.

Kingdom's product is a biologically derived ingredient, so Industrial Bio is the nearest match. The other options fit worse.

EduRev is a consumer learning app for students in India, which puts it in education. The fund's "Other" domain covers education, and none of the consumer subindustries (such as Job and Career Services or Content) describe it as well.

Trexo sells wearable robotic exoskeletons that help children with disabilities such as Cerebral Palsy walk. That is physical hardware worn on the body that directly assists a medical condition, which fits Medical Devices best.

Masterpiece sells short-term working capital, advancing cash against invoices and contracts, to businesses that supply training data to AI labs. That is a lending product, so Fintech and Credit and Lending is the best fit.

Blink is an AI app builder that serves builders, startups, and creators. It handles design, database, backend, hosting, and authentication, so its closest fit is a developer and product-team tool for building and shipping software. That points to B2B, Engineering, Product and Design.
Serra sells an AI recruiter to companies that want to hire: it automates candidate sourcing and outreach and delivers qualified interviews, which fits B2B, Recruiting and Talent.

Hadrius sells AI-driven securities compliance automation to regulated financial firms such as investment advisers. The buyers are businesses, and the product is compliance software, so the closest fits are Fintech (banking and compliance software) or B2B Legal (compliance). The Legal definition covers contract review, compliance, and in-house legal workflows. The Fintech "Banking and Exchange" definition explicitly mentions core banking and compliance software sold to financial institutions. Hadrius is focused on securities regulation for financial firms, which makes that the better fit.

Univerbal sells an AI language-learning app directly to individual consumers. The closest fit is Consumer, but none of the Consumer subindustries is an exact match. Job and Career Services covers professional skill-building, but this is general language learning. Home and Personal covers personal wellbeing and fitness instruction, so personal self-improvement tutoring fits there best. Education would normally land in Other, but because the product is a consumer app, I'm choosing Consumer.
PowerUs sells job-matching to individual blue-collar workers looking for better full-time jobs, which fits Consumer / Job and Career Services.

Vorticity sells a scientific computing platform to engineering and R&D teams in energy, life sciences and aerospace. These customers use it to run physics simulations before building expensive prototypes. The closest fit is the Industrials "Manufacturing and Robotics" subindustry, which covers engineering software for industrial operators. B2B Infrastructure (compute) and Analytics were also candidates, but the engineering-simulation focus points to Manufacturing and Robotics.

CentralComs sells AI agents to home services businesses (HVAC, plumbing, and similar) that handle call intake, dispatch, and scheduling. The buyer is a business, and the product automates internal workflows such as customer calls and job routing, so B2B Operations fits best. It isn't a tool built for a single function like sales or marketing, and it isn't a consumer product.

Fynn's core offering is private student loans for people attending trade school. That makes it a credit and lending product, so it fits Fintech and Credit and Lending better than Consumer Finance, which covers broader personal financial management.

Homebase sells rent-to-own financing to homebuyers in Southeast Asia, offering an alternative to high-interest mortgages. The core product is home financing, which makes it a lending business rather than a real estate marketplace. It fits Fintech, and within that, Credit and Lending.

FlatX is a rental marketplace that helps young renters in India find flats and flatmates without brokers. That fits Real Estate and Construction, in the Housing and Real Estate subindustry, which covers search tools and marketplaces for renters and landlords to find and manage already-built properties.
Perfectly sells an AI recruiting platform to startups that automates sourcing, outreach, screening, and qualification of candidates. That fits B2B, Recruiting and Talent.

GroundControl sells software to manufacturers, mainly in aerospace, defense and medical, that automates their regulated quality documentation. The closest fit is Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry, since the customers are manufacturers and the product automates their industrial workflows. B2B Operations was the main alternative, but the manufacturing focus points to Industrials.

Permitify sells AI software to city building departments and plan reviewers to check building plans against code and speed up permit issuance. That is software for planning, inspecting, and managing the construction of structures, including compliance, so it fits Real Estate and Construction → Construction best.

Mass Magnetics makes permanent magnets from recycled rare-earth scrap and sells them to defense, aerospace, and industrial manufacturers, who use them in motors, sensors, and other components. That makes it a materials and components supplier to industrial customers. Of the Industrials subindustries, Manufacturing and Robotics fits best, since it covers factory infrastructure sold to manufacturers and the company positions itself around robotics. Defense is a close alternative because of the DFARS-compliant magnets, but those magnets are a component input rather than a weapons system or protective equipment.

Pelica sells software, specifically AI agents and a data unification layer, to health plans, IPAs, MSOs, ACOs, and risk-bearing medical groups. Its tools handle quality performance, care gaps, and administrative workflows for those organizations. That fits Healthcare IT, which covers software and AI systems sold to providers and payers to manage clinical and operational workflows.

Conntour sells AI video-search and alerting software to organizations that run large camera networks, which makes it a B2B security product. The Defense and Industrials categories are about weapons and military hardware, which doesn't fit software sold to security teams.

Mudafy is a tech-enabled brokerage that helps people buy and sell already-built homes, so it fits Housing and Real Estate best. It serves homebuyers and sellers through virtual tours, online booking and pricing data, and gives agents tools to work faster.

Dashlabs.ai sells software to diagnostic laboratories and clinics, covering billing, booking, instrument integration and test result generation. That is software for managing clinical and administrative workflows at healthcare providers, so Healthcare IT fits better than Diagnostics, which is for companies selling the tests or assays themselves.
KaiPod Learning runs a network of microschools, which is education. None of the fund's sector-specific domains cover that, so it falls under Other.

Fort is a wearable device sold directly to individual consumers, which points to Consumer Electronics. Healthcare's Consumer Health and Wellness was the other candidate, but the product is a fitness-tracking gadget rather than a health or clinical service, so the hardware category fits better.

Mayflower sells to businesses' HR teams, and its product screens candidates for immigration eligibility and compliance within existing HR systems. The closest B2B subindustries are Human Resources, Recruiting and Talent, and Legal.

The product centers on screening global candidates and surfacing only compliant ones during hiring, which is a hiring-stage function. That points to Recruiting and Talent rather than broader HR record-keeping. It also generates attorney-ready forms, which touches Legal, but the buyer and workflow are HR hiring teams, so Legal is a weaker fit.

Basedash sells business intelligence software that lets business users build dashboards and analyze data from many sources using natural language. That puts it in B2B, and Analytics is the best-fit subindustry.
Zepto sells groceries directly to individual consumers via fast delivery, which fits the Consumer domain and the Food and Beverage subindustry (grocery and restaurant delivery services).
Voxel sells on-site solar generation and second-life battery storage systems to data centers, so I classified it under Industrials → Energy rather than a B2B software or infrastructure category.

Output Biosciences is an AI lab building biological intelligence for discovering new biology and designing therapeutics. The best fit is a research and computational platform sold to biotech and pharma, which matches Healthcare, Drug Discovery and Delivery. The description doesn't say they sell finished therapeutics themselves, so Therapeutics fits less well.

Upstream is an AI email assistant that sorts messages, drafts replies, follows up, and handles tasks like scheduling for the user. The pitch reads as a general-purpose tool for working faster across functions, not software for one department, so I'm classifying it under B2B Productivity.

Birch Biosciences sells engineered enzymes and a biomanufacturing process for recycling plastic. That fits Industrial Bio, which covers engineered organisms and biomanufacturing processes for non-therapeutic industrial uses such as chemical production. The alternative, Climate in Industrials, covers carbon reduction and emissions accounting products. I chose Industrial Bio because the core offering is the engineered enzyme technology itself, and the emissions reduction is a benefit of it.

Maximal sells load planning software to full truckload carriers, which is a logistics coordination tool for moving freight. That fits B2B, Supply Chain and Logistics. The alternative, Industrials/Automotive, covers vehicles and fleet technology, but Maximal sells planning software to carriers rather than vehicles or driving systems.

Rune is a consumer mobile app where friends talk over voice chat and play multiplayer games together. Developers also build games on its SDK, but the main product users pay attention to is the gaming platform. That fits Consumer, Gaming better than Social, because the core offering is gameplay.
RTHM operates a digital clinic that delivers care to patients with complex chronic conditions, so it sells care delivery services rather than software or devices. That fits Healthcare Services best.

Pharos sells AI software to hospitals that extracts facts from unstructured medical records to automate quality reporting. That fits Healthcare IT, since it is software for providers that manages clinical and administrative workflows rather than diagnosing or treating patients.
Docsum sells an AI contract repository and redlining tool to legal and finance teams, which fits the B2B Legal subindustry (contract review and in-house legal team workflows).

Maritime Fusion builds fusion reactors for ships and off-grid power, along with HTS cables for power distribution. That is power generation sold to shipping and energy customers, so Industrials > Energy fits better than Climate (which covers carbon capture and emissions accounting) or Automotive (which covers ground transportation).

DigiBuild sells to construction contractors, developers, and subcontractors, which points to Real Estate and Construction. Within that domain, Construction fits better than Housing and Real Estate because the product is a procurement and tracking tool for building materials used to build structures, not for buying or selling finished properties.

Mochi sells anime microdramas that people watch in the app, so the core offering is produced media for individual consumers. That fits Consumer, Content. The in-app creation tools are a secondary feature, and the main product is the shows themselves rather than interaction between users, which rules out Social.

Clau is a real estate marketplace and broker toolset for Mexico, so it falls under Housing and Real Estate. It sells property search, a broker CRM and mortgage brokerage to homebuyers, brokers and agents, which matches that subindustry's definition.

Care Weather builds and launches its own radar satellites and sells the weather data to governments and shipping companies. The Industrials "Aviation and Space" subindustry covers satellites and space-based data services sold to government agencies and commercial operators, which fits best.

Veritus sells AI agents for loan servicing and collections to consumer lenders. The buyers are lenders and financial institutions, so this is lending infrastructure and automation, which fits Fintech's Credit and Lending subindustry. The B2B Operations or Sales categories would fit a generic customer-support or outbound-calling tool, but Veritus is built specifically for lending.

Reframe is a consumer app sold directly to individuals for self-directed behavior change around drinking. That fits Healthcare's "Consumer Health and Wellness" subindustry, which covers wellness products and services sold directly to consumers for self-directed lifestyle improvement rather than clinical treatment by a provider.

Yassir is a consumer super app whose core offerings are ride-hailing and last-mile delivery, with financial services being added later. Ride-hailing is its primary business and is sold directly to individual consumers, so Transportation Services fits best.

Verdex sells AI claims verification technology to insurers, which fits Fintech and the Insurance subindustry, since that subindustry covers underwriting and risk-assessment technology sold to businesses. The agricultural customer base is secondary, because the buyer is the insurer.

Actipulse sells a physical brain stimulation device that treats depression and is moving through FDA trials. That fits Medical Devices, which covers hardware that treats a medical condition through interaction with the body.

Alpaca sells brokerage infrastructure through an API, letting developers and businesses offer stock and crypto trading to their customers. In the fund's definitions, "Banking and Exchange" covers crypto trading infrastructure and core banking software sold to financial institutions, which matches this best. "Asset Management" is about investment decision-making and portfolio tools, and Alpaca provides trading and custody infrastructure instead.

Nanograb sells an AI platform that designs targeted delivery vectors, meaning peptide binders attached to nanoparticles, for genetic medicines. This is a delivery technology for biotech and pharma customers rather than a finished therapeutic. That fits Healthcare, under Drug Discovery and Delivery.

Morada Uno underwrites and insures residential leases in Latin America, replacing the need for a guarantor. The core product is a rental guarantee, which is an insurance-like offering to landlords and brokers. That makes Fintech / Insurance the best fit, ahead of Real Estate / Housing.

Opusense AI sells report-writing software to construction field inspectors, inspection firms, and contractors. That places it in Real Estate and Construction, and the Construction subindustry covers tools sold to contractors, engineers, and inspectors to inspect or manage construction work.

REGENT builds all-electric seagliders, which are flying-boat vehicles sold to airlines and ferry companies. The closest fit is Industrials. Of the subindustries, Aviation and Space matches best because the product is an aircraft-like vehicle (a wing-in-ground-effect craft). Automotive is for ground transportation, and Drones covers only unmanned aircraft.

BluumBio sells engineered organisms and enzymes that break down pollution to industrial and environmental customers. That is non-therapeutic bioremediation, which matches the Healthcare "Industrial Bio" subindustry (engineered organisms and bio-based processes for industrial, agricultural, or environmental use). The Industrials "Climate" subindustry covers carbon reduction and emissions accounting, which is a weaker fit for toxic-chemical remediation.
Caretta sells real-time AI assistance to sales reps and revenue teams during live calls, which places it in B2B Sales.

Paces sells AI software and services to renewable energy and data center developers to speed up siting, interconnection, and permitting. The closest fits are Energy within Industrials and Construction within Real Estate and Construction. Its customers are power project developers, and the due-diligence tooling serves the development of energy infrastructure, so I classified it as Industrials, Energy.

Fondeadora is a digital bank for individual consumers in Mexico. It offers a mobile banking app and a debit card, so it sells deposit accounts. That fits Fintech, and within Fintech, the Banking and Exchange subindustry covers deposit accounts. Consumer Finance is the other candidate, but Fondeadora's core product is the bank account itself.

Medium Biosciences sells AI-designed affinity reagents, which are molecular tools such as binders and antibodies. Its customers are research teams and diagnostic developers. That points to Healthcare. Within Healthcare, the closest fit is Drug Discovery and Delivery, which covers research platforms and computational tools sold to biotech and pharma. Diagnostics is a weaker fit, because that category is for tests and assays that detect disease, and Medium sells the reagents that go into them.
Wanderlog is a consumer app for planning trips, covering itineraries, place discovery, and hotel booking. That fits Travel, Leisure and Tourism best.

Levro's core product is a multicurrency account for businesses to hold and convert 30+ currencies, which falls under Banking and Exchange. It also handles international payments, so Payments was a close alternative. Its emphasis on holding currency balances and low-cost FX conversion makes Banking and Exchange the better fit.

BuildJet sells a faster, cheaper CI runner cloud to developer teams that use GitHub Actions. The closest fit is B2B Infrastructure, since it provides compute that engineering teams run their builds on. Engineering, Product and Design is a plausible alternative, but the core offering is the compute cloud rather than a tool for building products.

Taskade is a general-purpose workspace that combines project management, AI agents, and automations, and lets teams build apps without code. Because it helps teams organize work and automate tasks across functions rather than serving one department, B2B Productivity fits best.

Nano sells an earned-wage-access and daily payroll product to employers (retailers and manufacturers) as a way to cut turnover and improve engagement. The buyer is the employer, and the product sits within payroll and workforce management. The closest fits are B2B Human Resources, which covers benefits, engagement and core HR records, and Fintech Payments or Credit and Lending. Because the pitch to the employer is about retention and a more engaged workforce, I'm classifying it as Human Resources.

Sensei sells robotic training data to robotics companies, using a hardware and software platform. The closest fit is Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry, since the customers are robotics developers and the product is data infrastructure for building robots. The main alternative was B2B Infrastructure, but the buyer and purpose are specific to robotics.

Surtr sells counter-drone software to military and security customers, which fits Defense best. The product is an operating system that fuses sensor data and recommends how to engage threats. Drones would apply to companies selling the drones themselves, and Surtr is defending against them.

Junction sells an API to health tech companies, so the closest fit is a developer-facing tool. Its customers are businesses that want to pull wearable data and order at-home lab tests through a single integration. Of the Healthcare options, Healthcare IT is the nearest, since it covers software and data infrastructure for providers and payers. Junction's buyers are health tech builders, though, so I chose B2B Engineering, Product and Design.

Tough Commerce sells a white-label commerce platform to construction material suppliers, producers and manufacturers. It covers order management, dispatching, logistics, e-ticketing and invoicing, so the buyer is a construction-industry business rather than a consumer. The closest fits are Real Estate and Construction (Construction), B2B Supply Chain and Logistics, or B2B Retail. I chose Construction because the pitch is "Shopify for construction" and the customers are construction suppliers.

Allowance's core product is a set of spend controls and one-time, scoped payment credentials that let AI agents pay on a user's behalf. That is payment infrastructure for transactions rather than account holding or lending, so Fintech / Payments fits best.

FlexDesk sells AI agents to corporate real estate teams at enterprises, to manage and optimize their office lease portfolios. Because the buyer is a company's internal facilities and real estate function rather than a homebuyer, renter, broker or agent, the Housing and Real Estate subindustry doesn't fit. The closest fit is B2B Office Management, which covers software for managing physical workspaces and facilities.

Synapticure delivers virtual clinical care and care coordination directly to patients and caregivers. The service is performed by people (clinicians and coordinators) rather than sold as software or hardware, so Healthcare Services fits best.

Margin sells a POS and operating system to liquor stores, which are retail merchants. That matches the B2B Retail subindustry, defined as software for retail, restaurant, or merchant businesses to manage storefronts and consumer-facing commerce operations.

MosaicVoice sells software to call centers that monitors customer conversations in real time and flags compliance violations. That is a business-facing tool for customer support operations, so I classified it as B2B Operations. Legal and Security were the other candidates, but the product is built around call center quality assurance and customer support workflow rather than legal work or system protection.

Clear is a free consumer mobile app for tracking skincare routines, products and selfies, with brand-agnostic recommendations and a community. That puts it closest to Consumer, Apparel and Cosmetics, which covers beauty and personal care products and the tools that power shopping for them. The data platform for clinicians and brands is a secondary aspect that doesn't outweigh the consumer product.

Envelope sells a consumer budgeting app with built-in checking and debit cards, aimed at individuals managing their everyday finances. That fits Fintech, Consumer Finance. Banking and Exchange was the closest alternative, but the main product is personal budgeting for individual consumers rather than deposit accounts as such.

Foundation sells software to homebuilders that handles online home shopping, purchase, and ownership. Its customers are builders, who are construction-industry companies, and its end users are homebuyers, so the two Real Estate and Construction subindustries are the candidates. "Housing and Real Estate" covers marketplaces and transaction services for buying, selling, or managing already-built properties, which fits the buying experience for new homes. "Construction" covers tools for planning, building, and managing the physical construction of structures. Foundation's product is a sales and buyer-facing platform rather than a construction-management tool, so I chose Housing and Real Estate.

Gather is a video chat platform where people meet, work, socialize, and learn in a shared virtual space. The category definitions place video meetings and tools for connecting people under Consumer / Social. Gather's spatial, avatar-based interface is not a VR/AR headset product, so Virtual and Augmented Reality fits less well.

Short Story is a consumer ecommerce and style discovery platform that sells clothing to petite women, which fits Consumer, Apparel and Cosmetics. That subindustry covers clothing sold directly to individuals, including through curated multi-brand storefronts.

Tank Payments sells payables automation to logistics businesses and a banking platform to trucking companies. This is primarily financial infrastructure for moving money, so Fintech fits best. Payments is the closest subindustry because the core product is payment processing and payables automation, with banking as a complement.

Glen sells a context and memory layer to companies that run AI coding agents. It's closest to the Infrastructure subindustry, which covers context and data handling systems that other software and engineering teams run on top of.

Maywood sells a proactive AI assistant to finance professionals (dealmakers such as bankers and investors). It tracks relationships and pipeline, drafts outreach, auto-updates CRMs, and prepares meeting briefs. The product is primarily about managing deals, relationships, and outreach, which is closest to a sales and pipeline tool for business users rather than a finance or accounting product.

Physical Turing deploys robots for industrial inspection and security tasks, which fits best under Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics (industrial automation and robots sold to industrial operators).

Miyagi Labs sells AI tutoring and exam prep directly to students, which is education. The fund's Other domain covers education, and none of the Consumer subindustries (such as Job and Career Services, which is about employment and professional skills) fits standardized-exam prep for students.

Ohmic Biosciences engineers disease-resistance genes for crops, which it sells to growers and agribusinesses. That fits Industrials, Agriculture, whose definition covers plant biology and pesticide-discovery tools for growers and agribusinesses. Industrial Bio under Healthcare covers non-therapeutic biomanufacturing, but the focus here is crop protection, so Agriculture is the better match.

CoCrafter sells a B2B marketplace and management tools to contractors and subcontractors in construction, so it fits Real Estate and Construction. Within that domain, Construction fits better than Housing and Real Estate, which covers buying, selling, or renting already-built properties.

Stable sells a virtual business address and mailroom to startups, covering mail handling and guidance on compliantly switching a company's address. That is a back-office service for businesses, so it belongs in B2B. Of the B2B subindustries, Operations fits best because this is internal administrative workflow, not finance, HR, or legal software. Office Management is a close alternative since it covers physical workspaces and logistics, but Stable is a virtual, software-driven mailroom for remote startups and not a tool for managing a physical office.

Lucid Bots sells cleaning drones and ground-based pressure-washing robots to B2B customers. The closest fits are Drones (the flagship product is a cleaning drone) and Manufacturing and Robotics (industrial robots). The Drones subindustry covers unmanned aerial vehicles and drone-enabled inspection services sold to commercial customers, and the main product is a drone, so I chose Drones.
Qlo sells AI underwriting software to commercial insurance carriers, so Fintech → Insurance fits best. The Insurance subindustry covers underwriting and risk-assessment technology.

CopyCat sells AI software to insurance brokers and agencies. Fintech's Insurance subindustry covers brokerage services and underwriting technology, so that is the best fit. B2B Operations or Legal were the alternatives, but the product is built specifically for insurance brokerage workflows.

Nori is a humanoid mobile manipulator robot sold to both homes and businesses. The closest fit is Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry, which covers robots and industrial automation systems. The consumer-facing use cases (cleaning, folding clothes) are real, but the company's core product is robotics hardware plus a data and training platform, so I'm not classifying it under Consumer Electronics.

Shef is a marketplace where consumers order homemade meals from local chefs and have them delivered. That is an edible product sold directly to individual consumers, so it fits Consumer, Food and Beverage.
Albedo builds and operates satellites and sells VLEO imagery and space infrastructure to government and commercial customers, which fits Industrials, Aviation and Space.

Pluto's main customers are companies that pay to find and reach candidates, and professionals use it for free to build a profile. That makes it a tool for sourcing and hiring talent, so Recruiting and Talent in B2B fits better than the Consumer Job and Career Services category.

The company offers employer-backed salary advances and bill payments to employees, which makes it a financial-wellness product aimed at individual employees. Earned wage access is a form of credit, but the pitch centers on broader financial wellness (saving, spending, budgeting and borrowing). That fits Consumer Finance better than Credit and Lending, which is focused specifically on providing loans.

Pagaloop's core product is a payment-facilitation service. It lets businesses and individuals pay third parties, such as landlords, tax authorities and suppliers, with a credit card, even when those payees don't accept cards. That makes Payments a better fit than Credit and Lending, because Pagaloop takes no underwriting risk and the credit stays with the card issuer.

WeReno sells AI agents that coordinate renovations and project work for homeowners, contractors and commercial property owners. Its products span consumer repairs, renovation management, a contractor back office and commercial capital projects. The strongest common thread is that it serves the construction and renovation workflow, so I classified it under Real Estate and Construction, Construction.

UNISON is building a headset for virtual and mixed reality, so the best fit is the Consumer domain, under Virtual and Augmented Reality. That subindustry excludes devices whose main purpose is immersive VR/AR, so Consumer Electronics does not apply.

Lizza sells an AI assistant to D2C e-commerce brands that finds, contacts, and manages content creators for collaborations. This is influencer marketing software, so it fits B2B Marketing, which covers customer acquisition through campaigns and outbound messaging.

Cascade Space sells deep space communications and tracking services, a commercial ground station network. Its customers are space agencies and commercial space operators, so it fits Industrials, Aviation and Space.

Retrofit sells vintage clothing and accessories directly to individual shoppers through a curated marketplace, so it fits Consumer, Apparel and Cosmetics. The AI curation is how it picks and personalizes inventory, but what the customer buys is physical apparel.

Pair Team runs a medical group and delivers care coordination services (community health workers, social needs support) to Medicaid and Medicare patients. The core offering is care delivery performed by people, which fits Healthcare Services best, even though they plan to add an AI care manager.

Ansa sells enzymatic DNA synthesis, which is a tool and platform for researchers and biotech companies. The closest fit is Healthcare, in the Drug Discovery and Delivery subindustry, which covers research platforms sold to biotech and pharma companies. Industrial Bio was the other candidate, but Ansa's customers are mainly biological researchers and therapeutics developers rather than industrial producers.

Codingal sells online coding and AI classes for kids and teens (Grades 1-12), so it is an education company. The fund's "Other" domain explicitly covers education. The Consumer subindustries focus on career skills, content, and similar offerings, and none of them fits K-12 education.

General Legal is an AI-enabled law firm that sells legal services to high-growth companies, covering commercial, corporate and employment law. The B2B Legal subindustry covers software or services sold to businesses or law firms for legal work, so it fits best.
Corgi is a full-stack insurance carrier that underwrites and issues policies directly to startups, so Fintech → Insurance fits best.

Vision Lab sells training data, built from first-person industrial video and process knowledge, to robotics and AI labs. The closest fit is Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry, because the data comes from real factory workflows and is meant to help train industrial robots. The other candidate was a B2B subindustry such as Analytics or Infrastructure, but the focus on factory data and robotics points to Manufacturing and Robotics.

Cash Flow Portal sells investor-management software to real estate syndicators. It handles subscription docs, wire instructions and investor communication, and that is fundraising and investor-relations workflow rather than property search or construction.

The closest fits were Fintech Asset Management and Real Estate and Construction Housing and Real Estate. I chose Asset Management because the product manages investor capital relationships for fund sponsors, not the buying, selling or renting of properties.

Cardinal Gray sells software to lenders (financial institutions) that automates lien filings with the DMV for auto loans. The customers are lenders, and the product is lending-operations automation, so Fintech's Credit and Lending subindustry fits best, since its definition includes lending infrastructure and automation sold to financial institutions.

Roame is a flight search tool sold directly to travelers to help them redeem credit card points and miles for trips. Its core offering is trip search and booking for consumers, so it fits Travel, Leisure and Tourism better than Consumer Finance, even though it touches fintech through credit card points.
SFA Therapeutics develops oral drugs for autoimmune diseases and inflammation-driven cancers and has run clinical trials, so it sells therapeutics.

Brickwise sells to landlords and estate agents who manage already-built properties, so Real Estate and Construction is the best-fitting domain. Within it, Housing and Real Estate fits because the product serves property managers and landlords, not construction companies.

MedMe sells web-based software to pharmacies, both independents and chains, for scheduling, virtual care, documentation automation, and flagging clinical opportunities. Its customers are healthcare provider organizations and the product is software, so Healthcare IT fits best.

Rarebird sells coffee, a drink, directly to consumers who are sensitive to caffeine. The paraxanthine replacement is an ingredient in that drink, so Food and Beverage fits better than Consumer Health and Wellness.

Moneco is a neobank for underserved migrant communities in Europe. It offers a current account, a payment card and free remittances to individual consumers. The best fit is Fintech, and within it Consumer Finance, since it serves an underserved demographic and aims to become a one-stop shop for everyday financial needs. Banking and Exchange was the closest alternative, but the consumer-facing, demographic-focused positioning points to Consumer Finance.

Slicker sells payment failure recovery to subscription businesses. Its AI-powered retries target involuntary churn from failed recurring payments. That fits Fintech Payments, which covers transaction processing and fraud prevention infrastructure for businesses.

Peoplebox.ai sells to businesses, so it falls under B2B. It has two product lines. One is an AI interviewer for pre-screens and first-round interviews, which is recruiting. The other is a talent management suite covering OKRs, performance reviews, career growth, calibration and compensation, which is core HR. The one-liner leads with "hire, manage, and grow your people", and the talent management suite is the larger part of the platform, so Human Resources fits better than Recruiting and Talent.

Spot Health sells a white-labeled, API-driven platform to brands, covering at-home collection kits, logistics, physician authorization, and lab integrations. Its product is diagnostic testing infrastructure, so Diagnostics fits best. Healthcare IT and Healthcare Services are close, but the core offering is the lab-analyzed tests themselves.

Circleback sells AI meeting notes, action items, search and automations to teams across functions. That is general-purpose software for organizing knowledge and automating tasks, which fits B2B Productivity better than a single-department category like Sales or Operations.

FLOWER CO. sells legal cannabis directly to individual consumers online, with next-day delivery. Of the consumer subindustries, Food and Beverage fits best, since cannabis is an edible or consumable product sold and delivered to individuals for personal consumption.

Community Phone sells a physical phone, along with a family app, directly to consumers, mainly adult children buying for their aging parents. The best fit is Consumer Electronics. Healthcare and Social were also candidates, but the core product is a consumer hardware device rather than a clinical service or an interpersonal platform.
Durate sells scheduling software to physician groups, clinics, and hospitals. That is software for managing a provider's operational workflow, which fits Healthcare IT.

Weel is a free smartphone app for individual drivers that combines a dashcam, navigation and driver-assistance features. This is a consumer product, and the closest fit is Transportation Services, which covers tools for navigating transportation infrastructure and vehicle ownership. Consumer Electronics doesn't fit because Weel sells software rather than hardware.

Bloom is a consumer investing app that combines financial education with an investing account. The closest fit is Fintech, and within it, Asset Management, since it sells investing tools and platforms to individual investors. Consumer Finance was the main alternative, but the investing account at the center of the product points to Asset Management.
Bolster is a platform for contractors, subcontractors, retailers and consumers to buy, sell and manage residential construction projects, so the Construction subindustry fits best.

Hesper AI sells AI claims-investigation software to insurance carriers, MGAs and TPAs. The best fit is Fintech, Insurance, because the subindustry covers underwriting and risk-assessment technology sold to insurers. The alternative would be Healthcare IT or B2B Operations, but the product is built specifically for insurance claims workflows.

Littio is a neobank selling dollar-denominated savings accounts, debit cards, and investing options directly to individuals in Latin America. That puts it in Fintech. Within Fintech, "Banking and Exchange" fits best, since the core offering is deposit accounts and currency exposure. "Consumer Finance" is the closest alternative, but the product is mainly account holding rather than broader financial planning.

Epsilon3 sells ERP, MES, and test management software to manufacturers and engineering operations teams in aerospace, energy, defense, maritime, and biotech. Its buyers are industrial operators, and the product automates their manufacturing and operations workflows, which fits Industrials / Manufacturing and Robotics. B2B / Operations was the other candidate, but the focus on manufacturing execution and factory-style workflows points to Industrials.

Shinkei sells robotic systems to fishing boats and fish farms. The robots automate the humane slaughter and handling of fish so the meat lasts longer and tastes better. Its customers are harvesters and farmers, which are producers rather than consumers. The closest fit is Industrials, in the Agriculture subindustry, which covers food production systems sold to growers and food producers. Manufacturing and Robotics is the other candidate, but that subindustry is aimed at factory automation.

Plena sells AI software to specialty medical practices to automate administrative workflows such as referrals, fax intake, scheduling, compliance, and collections. That matches Healthcare IT, which covers software sold to healthcare providers to manage their clinical, financial, or operational workflows.

Pledge Health sells AI software to clinics and healthcare administrative teams that automates revenue cycle management work on payer portals. That matches the Healthcare IT definition: software sold to providers to manage administrative and financial workflows.

Avelis sells machine-learning software that audits medical claims for self-insured employers and health plans, which are payers rather than care providers. That fits Healthcare IT, which covers software and AI sold to providers and payers to manage administrative and financial workflows.

I considered Insurance (underwriting and risk-assessment technology) as an alternative. Avelis does claims payment integrity, not underwriting or policy sales, so Healthcare IT fits better.

SureBright sells product warranties, an insurance-like offering, through an embedded checkout platform. Merchants get the revenue, but the core product is warranty underwriting and pricing, so Fintech / Insurance fits best.

Greypoint builds drone swarms for military use that locate and track enemy radio emitters, so the product is sold to defense customers for combat and surveillance. Defense fits better than Drones, because the drones are a means to a military end, and the Drones category is aimed at commercial, government, and emergency-response drone use.

Fetii is a group ride-sharing service that moves people in high-capacity vehicles, sold directly to individual riders. That puts it in Consumer, under Transportation Services, which covers ride-sharing and carpooling.

Zephyr Fusion is building a megawatt-class fusion reactor for use in orbit. The closest fits are Energy (power generation) and Aviation and Space (space infrastructure sold to commercial space operators). The product is a power generation source, but its entire purpose is to power industry in space, and the customers are commercial space operators. I picked Aviation and Space because the space operating environment defines both the product and the buyers.

Hop Aero builds rocket cargo vehicles for the U.S. and its allies to deliver supplies into contested environments, which points to a defense customer base. The closest fit is Industrials, in the Defense subindustry. Aviation and Space and Drones are less fitting, since the product is a point-to-point rocket delivery system for military logistics rather than a spacecraft, satellite or UAV.

Alguna sells quote-to-cash software (CPQ, invoicing, usage-based billing) to B2B companies, and its main buyers are finance and revenue operations teams. Among the B2B subindustries, Finance and Accounting fits best because invoicing, billing, and collections are accounts-receivable work. Sales (quoting and pricing) and Fintech Payments are close alternatives, but billing and revenue automation is the core of the product.

Interfaze sells an AI model to developers and companies for tasks like document intelligence, object detection, and classification. That makes it a developer-facing building block, so Engineering, Product and Design fits better than Infrastructure, Analytics, or Productivity.
Orca Aerospace sells onboard AI software that operates spacecraft and satellites, so it fits Industrials, Aviation and Space, where customers are space operators and aerospace firms.

VotingWorks is a non-profit that builds open-source voting machines and sells them to government election offices. That is a government and civic-infrastructure business, and none of the six sector domains (B2B, Consumer, Fintech, Healthcare, Industrials, Real Estate and Construction) describes it well. The "Other" domain explicitly covers government and nonprofits, so I'm classifying it there.

Mailwarm sells email warmup and deliverability tools to businesses doing email marketing and cold outreach, so Marketing is the closest fit. Its main goal is getting outbound messages into the inbox rather than managing sales deals.

Marketfeed helps individual Indians understand and fix their personal finances, which points to Fintech and Consumer Finance. The company sells directly to consumers, and its focus is broad personal financial decision-making rather than loans, payments, or investment management specifically.

Flick is software that individual filmmakers and creators use to make AI-generated short films. The closest fit is Consumer, and within it, Content: the product is a creation tool, but the company also produces its own films and builds a community around them. The alternatives fit less well. B2B Productivity or Engineering, Product and Design would suit a tool sold to teams, and Virtual and Augmented Reality is about immersive 3D, which this is not.

KubeSail sells home-hosting hardware (PiBox) and software for individuals to self-host apps, and also a platform for companies to deploy their software on demand for their customers. The core product is deployment tooling that other software runs on, which fits B2B Infrastructure better than Consumer Electronics.

Benepass sells a benefits platform to HR teams, but the product itself is a payments card and app. The company describes itself as fintech for corporate compensation and runs its own payments stack. The closest fits were Human Resources (B2B), Consumer Finance, and Payments. I chose Human Resources because the buyer is the company's HR team and the product handles employee benefits administration, which the Human Resources definition covers. Payments and Consumer Finance are weaker matches since the card is only the delivery mechanism and employees aren't the purchasers.
Helonic sells software to construction teams that analyzes PDF drawings, detects clashes across disciplines, and drafts RFIs. That fits Real Estate and Construction, in the Construction subindustry.
The Juggernaut sells subscription media (articles and editorial content) directly to individual consumers, so it fits Consumer, Content.

Cocreate sells video production and post-production software to editors, assistants, DITs, post supervisors, and UPMs, who are professionals working in the field. Because it is a tool for those professionals' workflows, B2B fits better than Consumer. Within B2B, Productivity is the best match. It helps teams organize footage and notes and cuts down on menial tasks, and it isn't built for a single department like finance or HR.

o11 sells an AI data warehouse to financial firms. It unifies their CRM, email, files and market data and produces business intelligence from it. The closest fit is B2B Analytics, since the product is about modeling and unifying business data for decision-makers. Infrastructure was the other candidate, but the pitch centers on the intelligence the data produces rather than on compute or access-management building blocks.

Innate builds general-purpose personal robots that individuals and developers can teach by code, language and demonstration, which is hardware and software for robotics. The closest fit is Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry. The alternative was Consumer Electronics, but the platform is aimed at developers and general robotics rather than a single-purpose consumer gadget.

Metreecs sells AI demand forecasting software to retailers for planning, buying, and allocating products. The closest fits are B2B Retail, B2B Supply Chain and Logistics, and B2B Analytics. Retail covers software for merchants' consumer-facing commerce operations, while Supply Chain and Logistics is about moving goods between suppliers, carriers, and buyers. Metreecs is inventory planning and merchandising for retailers, not logistics, so I chose Retail.

Alga Biosciences sells a product to cattle producers that cuts methane from cows. The two closest fits are Agriculture (livestock products sold to growers and producers) and Climate (emissions reduction). Because the customer is the cattle industry and the product is a livestock feed intervention, I chose Agriculture.

ValCtrl is a prediction market where users trade on beliefs about the future, so it sells trading access to individual investors and traders. That fits Fintech, and Banking and Exchange is the closest subindustry because it covers trading infrastructure and exchange-style products. Asset Management is about investment decision-making and portfolio tools, and Gaming includes wagering platforms but fits less well here since the product is a priced, market-making exchange.
Redbird sells an enterprise analytics platform that handles data prep, analysis and reporting, so it fits B2B, Analytics.

Grip sells robotic sorting systems to waste and recycling operators, which are industrial automation products. That fits Industrials, and Manufacturing and Robotics is the closest subindustry. Climate was the other candidate, but the offering is robots that automate sorting rather than carbon reduction or emissions accounting.

Apero Health sells medical billing software to healthcare practices, covering eligibility, claims, and patient payments, and integrates with EHRs. That is software for the administrative and financial workflows of healthcare providers, so Healthcare IT fits best.

xPay sells SaaS companies a way to handle international billing, sales tax compliance, and payment acceptance. The core offering is commerce infrastructure for processing payments and handling the compliance around them, so I'm classifying it as Fintech, Payments. The closest alternative is B2B Finance and Accounting, but the payment acceptance and merchant-of-record style tax remittance point to Payments.

Serif Health sells healthcare price transparency data products and APIs, which are software and data infrastructure for healthcare payers, providers, and related organizations. That fits Healthcare IT best, since the other healthcare options cover clinical products or services rather than data tools.

Dayra's core offering is embedded loans and earnings advances, delivered through an API that businesses plug into their own apps, with virtual bank accounts as a secondary product. That makes Credit and Lending the best fit, since lending infrastructure sold to businesses is its main product.
Binks is a factory-to-consumer apparel company that sells made-to-measure clothing directly to individual women in India, so it fits the Consumer domain under Apparel and Cosmetics.

Thrive Agric sells to farmers in Africa: inputs financing, extension services, and a marketplace for agro-commodities. Its customers are growers and agribusinesses, and its core offering is farm-management and crop production support, so Industrials / Agriculture fits best. Fintech (lending) is a secondary element, but the main focus is the agricultural value chain.

Arpeggio Bio is a pharmaceutical company that develops its own drug candidates. Its lead program is heading toward a development candidate for melanoma, and it also cites a Phase I success. Because it sells therapeutics rather than research platforms to other biotechs, Therapeutics fits better than Drug Discovery and Delivery.

Sendbox sells fulfillment and logistics services to e-commerce merchants, which makes it a B2B company. Within B2B, Supply Chain and Logistics fits best because it covers moving physical goods between merchants, carriers, and buyers.
Jenfi sells revenue-based financing to growing digital businesses, so its core product is capital, which fits Fintech and the Credit and Lending subindustry.

Rescript sells an AI platform for tracking and interpreting regulations to law firms, corporations, and trade associations. That is a legal and compliance product for businesses, so it fits B2B, Legal.

Dreamscale Labs sells a cloud inference platform that robotics developers run on top of, so it is a technical building block rather than an end-user application. That fits B2B Infrastructure better than Industrials Manufacturing and Robotics, since the customers are robotics teams buying compute rather than manufacturers buying automation systems.

Circular rents consumer electronics (smartphones, laptops, headphones, wearables) to individual consumers on a monthly subscription. The Consumer Electronics subindustry explicitly covers companies that "design, manufacture, or rent physical hardware devices for individual consumer use", so that is the best fit.

WANTD runs a consumer-facing marketplace for fashion and footwear. Brands use it to launch and sell product through live commerce, auctions and influencer networks, with fulfillment handled for them. The closest fit is Consumer, Apparel and Cosmetics, because the offering centers on selling clothing and footwear to individual shoppers. The alternative is a B2B Retail tool for merchants, like Shopify, but WANTD describes itself as a marketplace rather than storefront software.

Palmier Pro is a video editor that AI agents such as Claude and Codex can operate directly. It is free and open-source, and it's used to make launch videos, so its buyers are likely creators and teams producing video content rather than a single consumer group. The closest fit is B2B Productivity, since it is general-purpose software that helps people work faster. Consumer Content was the main alternative, but that category is for selling produced media to viewers, which doesn't apply to an editing tool.

Rudus sells AI takeoff and estimation software to concrete contractors, so it fits Real Estate and Construction. Within that domain, Construction is the better match because the product helps contractors plan and bid physical construction work, rather than helping buyers or agents transact on already-built properties.

Lumeria sells a consumer hardware device (a phone-clip multispectral camera) plus software for at-home skin scanning, tracking, and product matching. The buyer is the individual consumer, and the focus is skincare and self-directed wellness rather than clinical diagnosis. The closest fits were Consumer Health and Wellness, Apparel and Cosmetics (beauty and personal care) and Consumer Electronics. I chose Consumer Health and Wellness because the product's core value is personal skin-health insight.

Cinder sells trust and safety infrastructure to businesses. Its platform covers content moderation, abuse investigation, and AI safety, which fits B2B Security best, since the focus is protecting systems and communities from abuse.
