Storyboarder is a platform where anyone can create, share, and sell webcomics, and readers consume the finished comics. That puts the core offering closest to consumer content, with creators and readers as the individual users. It could also be read as a B2B creative tool, but the focus on publishing and selling webcomics to readers makes Content the better fit.

Chowdeck is a consumer-facing food delivery marketplace where individuals order meals from restaurants and have them delivered. That matches the Consumer domain's Food and Beverage subindustry, which covers grocery and restaurant delivery services sold directly to individual consumers.

Bayesline sells a GPU-powered financial analytics suite to institutional investors such as hedge funds. The two candidate domains are Fintech (Asset Management) and B2B (Analytics). The Asset Management definition covers investment management and portfolio construction tools and platforms for funds and institutions. Bayesline's product is analytics built for asset managers to generate alpha, which fits that definition more closely than generic business analytics.

PerfectBit builds learned manipulation and control policies for robots, which it sells as robotics automation technology. That fits Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry, which covers robots and automation systems for physical workflows.

Overview.ai sells custom hardware, edge AI, and software for quality inspection and defect detection to manufacturers. That matches Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics, which covers industrial automation systems and factory infrastructure sold to manufacturers.

FleetWorks sells an AI-enabled freight marketplace that matches trucks with jobs. This is software and a platform for coordinating logistics between shippers, brokers, and carriers. That fits B2B, Supply Chain and Logistics rather than Industrials, Automotive, which covers vehicles and driving systems.

Hamming AI sells testing and monitoring software to teams building voice agents. That makes its customers developers and product teams, so Engineering, Product and Design is the closest fit among the B2B subindustries.

Micora sells deployable solar microgrid systems to commercial and utility-scale customers for power generation, so Industrials / Energy fits best. It could also be read as construction, but the product is the power generation hardware itself rather than software or services for construction firms.

Axle Health sells scheduling and workforce management software to home healthcare providers, so it fits Healthcare IT, which covers software sold to providers for managing their operational workflows. The B2B Operations category is a poorer fit because the customers are healthcare providers and the product is built around their clinical scheduling and dispatching.

Oto sells a digital program that helps individual patients manage tinnitus, delivering therapy that was previously only available through in-person specialists. This is a self-directed digital health product sold to consumers. It is not a medical device, a diagnostic tool, or a service performed by people, so Consumer Health and Wellness fits best.

EARTH AI is a mineral exploration company. It uses AI to predict where critical metal deposits are and its own drilling technology to test those sites. It sells exploration and discovery of metal deposits rather than software to a specific business function. The closest fit among the available categories is Industrials. Within Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics (industrial automation and factory infrastructure) and Climate (carbon reduction) don't match well. Energy covers power generation and grid infrastructure, not mining.

The nearest option is Energy, since critical metals support the energy transition and resource production. Manufacturing and Robotics is a weaker fit because it covers engineering software and automation for industrial operators, which is a loose match for AI exploration and drilling technology.

I'll go with Manufacturing and Robotics, since the drilling technology and AI tools are used by industrial operators in resource extraction.

Pivot Robotics sells AI software for robotic arms to manufacturers, starting with metal grinding in foundries. That is industrial automation sold to manufacturers, which fits Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics.
Outship sells a technical assessment tool to companies that hire engineers. It records and analyzes how candidates work with AI coding tools, so it fits Recruiting and Talent within B2B.

Aviron sells connected rowing machines with built-in games directly to consumers. The closest fit is Consumer, since the buyer is an individual. Within Consumer, "Home and Personal" explicitly covers fitness instruction and personal wellbeing, which matches a home-fitness product. "Consumer Electronics" is the main alternative, but the core offering is the fitness and entertainment experience rather than a general gadget. "Gaming" and "Virtual and Augmented Reality" fit less well, because the games serve the workout rather than being the product.

Shimmer sells 1:1 ADHD coaching directly to individuals. The coaching is delivered by people rather than software, and it is aimed at personal wellbeing and self-improvement rather than clinical treatment. The closest fit is Consumer Health and Wellness within Healthcare. Healthcare Services was the other candidate, but coaching is not clinical care, and the product is sold straight to consumers for lifestyle improvement.

Gojiberry sells AI agents that run outbound sales for B2B companies: finding buyers, reaching out, following up, and booking meetings. That fits B2B Sales, which covers outbound selling and revenue operations, better than Marketing, which is about top-of-funnel demand generation.

Clad sells project management and billing software to contractors and operators building infrastructure such as internet and power networks. That fits Real Estate and Construction, in the Construction subindustry, which covers software for contractors to plan, build, and manage construction work.

Hebbian Robotics sells data-evaluation and quality-control pipelines, delivered through code and custom models, to teams building physical AI and robotics. That makes it a developer-facing tool rather than robotics hardware. Of the available categories, "Engineering, Product and Design" fits best, since it covers tools used to build and ship software products. "Infrastructure" and "Analytics" are plausible alternatives, but the product is aimed at developers building AI systems.
Leadbay sells lead qualification and prospecting software to B2B sales teams, so it fits under B2B Sales.

Invertix deploys custom AI models inside energy and critical-infrastructure operators, using SCADA and operational data to make their operations more efficient. Its customers are utilities and industrial energy operators, so the Energy subindustry under Industrials fits best.

OS3 sells humanoid robots and the AI behind them to businesses such as hotels, hospitals, and labs, to automate repetitive physical work. That fits Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry, which covers robots and industrial automation systems sold to operators.
Alixia is developing drug compounds that treat cancer by targeting the tumor microenvironment, which makes it a therapeutics company.

Stipop's current positioning is a Patreon-like monetization platform for independent character creators, which sells to individual consumers and fans. It also offers a sticker API and SDK to chat apps, which is a B2B developer product.

The core offering is a creator marketplace where fans consume and support character IP. That makes Consumer the best fit. Within Consumer, Content (creator-produced media sold directly to individuals) fits better than Social, since the value is consuming and supporting character content rather than interpersonal connection.

Valence is a trading platform that aggregates and executes contracts across prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket. It is aimed at systematic traders and offers APIs and backtesting tools. That makes it trading infrastructure rather than a payments or lending product. I placed it in Fintech under Banking and Exchange, whose description covers trading infrastructure. Asset Management was the other candidate, but that category is about investment decision-making and portfolio tools, which fits less well.

MedCrypt sells a cybersecurity toolkit to medical device vendors. It handles threat detection, regulatory compliance, and threat sharing between vendors. The product is security software sold to businesses, not a medical device, so I classified it under B2B Security rather than Healthcare.
Florin is a full-stack insurance carrier that uses a model to underwrite, price, and quote policies, so it fits Fintech and the Insurance subindustry.

Bidflow sells AI estimating and takeoff software to electrical contractors, helping them bid on construction jobs faster. That is software for contractors to plan and estimate construction work, so it fits Real Estate and Construction, Construction.

Kivo Health delivers virtual care directly to seniors with chronic lung disease, working with health systems and payers. The offering is care delivered by people and supported by AI, rather than software or hardware sold to providers, so Healthcare Services fits best.

Waza sells a B2B cross-border payments platform to businesses in emerging markets, covering global payments, treasury and liquidity. The core product moves money for transactions, so Fintech → Payments fits better than Banking and Exchange, which centers on holding accounts or exchanging currency.

Nest Genomics sells software to healthcare organizations for running genomic programs. The platform handles consent and counseling, EMR-integrated clinical decision support, and care management. That fits Healthcare IT, which covers software sold to providers and payers for clinical and operational workflows. Diagnostics is a weaker fit because Nest is lab-agnostic and does not sell the tests themselves.

Machine26 is a marketplace where construction machine owners sell used equipment to dealers. The customers are construction businesses and dealers, so the fit is Real Estate and Construction rather than consumer or supply chain. Within that domain, Construction is the better subindustry because the offering serves construction companies and suppliers. Housing and Real Estate covers already-built properties, which doesn't apply here.

Degla sells software that turns natural-language goals into autonomous multi-drone missions, which fits Industrials, Drones. That subindustry covers drone navigation and ground-control systems sold to commercial and government customers.

Consus sells an API that routes AI requests to compliant infrastructure, so aerospace and defense companies can use AI with ITAR or CUI data. The buyers are businesses, and the product is a developer-facing building block that handles compliance and backend work. That makes it a B2B company, and Infrastructure fits better than Security or Engineering tools because the core offering is compliant infrastructure and compliance handling that applications run on top of.

Verdant sells AI agents to local governments, starting with permitting workflows. Its customers are government agencies, which fits the "Other" domain (education, government, nonprofits). The permitting focus could suggest Real Estate and Construction, but the buyer is the government and the product is general government efficiency software, so "Other" fits best.
Dawn Industries sells software to manufacturers that diagnoses and fixes faults in industrial automation cells (PLCs, robots, CNC machines), which fits Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics.

Origin sells patient-derived cancer datasets (spatial transcriptomics, H&E images and clinical labels) to pharmaceutical and AI companies for R&D. This fits Healthcare, and within it Drug Discovery and Delivery, which covers research platforms and tools sold to biotech and pharma companies for identifying and designing drug candidates. Diagnostics doesn't fit because the data isn't used to diagnose patients, and Healthcare IT doesn't fit because it isn't workflow software for providers.

Manara connects Middle East software engineers with global tech jobs by offering interview preparation and referrals. Its core user is the individual job seeker, so it fits Consumer, in Job and Career Services. It also serves global tech companies that want to hire, which could point to B2B Recruiting and Talent. The candidate-facing placement and career-prep offering is the main product, so I chose Consumer.

Latent sells AI software to health systems that automates administrative work such as prior authorizations by analyzing EHR records. That is software for healthcare providers' operational workflows, so it fits Healthcare IT.

Palla is a consumer remittance app. US senders move money to recipients in other countries, which is money transfer infrastructure, so Fintech → Payments is the best fit. Banking and Exchange covers holding accounts and currency exchange rather than moving money for transactions.

Volopay sells a spend management platform to businesses, covering corporate cards, bill payments, expense approvals, and accounting reconciliation. Its buyers are finance and accounting teams, which points to B2B Finance and Accounting. The alternative is Fintech Payments, but the product is mainly spend control and reconciliation software for finance teams, so Finance and Accounting is the closer fit.

Ever Loved sells directly to families, helping them plan and pay for funerals: fundraising, vendor discovery, and memorial communication. That is a personal service for individual consumers, so it fits Consumer. Within Consumer, the closest subindustry is Home and Personal, which covers personal errands and wellbeing services for individuals.

DocVita sells telehealth consultations and concierge care coordination directly to patients in India, so I classed it as Healthcare Services. The care is delivered by people (doctors and concierges) rather than through software or hardware.

Pandai is a learning app for school students, so it is an education product. The fund's domains have no education category, and the "Other" domain explicitly covers education. The Consumer "Job and Career Services" subindustry is about employment and career skills, which does not fit school-age curriculum learning.

AveryIQ sells AI leasing and maintenance agents to property managers and landlords, so the closest fit is Real Estate and Construction. Within that domain, "Housing and Real Estate" covers tools sold to landlords and agents to market, lease, and manage already-built properties, which matches Avery's work on filling vacancies, scheduling tours, and handling tenant requests.

Libra Robotics sells robotic crews to infrastructure construction projects such as solar farms and data centers. The buyer is a construction company, so Real Estate and Construction fits better than Industrials' Manufacturing and Robotics. Within that domain, the Construction subindustry matches because the product is tools for building physical structures.

Callab AI sells AI voice agents to call centers and enterprises, which automate customer calls on their existing phone systems. That is business software for customer support operations, so it falls under B2B Operations, whose description covers customer support workflows.

Propaya sells AI document-extraction and risk-tracking software to commercial real estate teams, such as property managers, legal teams and portfolio owners, to manage already-built properties. That fits Real Estate and Construction, and its customers are landlords, managers and brokers rather than builders, so the best subindustry is Housing and Real Estate. Legal was a possible alternative because it parses leases, but the product is aimed at real estate portfolio management.

PayMongo is a payment processing company. It sells payment acceptance infrastructure (APIs, plugins, and support for cards, e-wallets and over-the-counter payments) to businesses and individuals in the Philippines, which fits Fintech and the Payments subindustry.

Blueshoe is a law firm that sells legal guidance and representation directly to individual consumers and plaintiffs. That points to Consumer, and the closest subindustry is Home and Personal, which explicitly covers personal legal services such as legal document preparation. The B2B Legal category is aimed at businesses and law firms, so it fits less well here.

Udhaar App is a bookkeeping app that micro SMEs use to track store credit, sales, and cash management. That fits the B2B Finance and Accounting subindustry, which covers software that businesses use for bookkeeping and financial management.

The Context Company sells analytics for production AI agents. It analyzes every customer conversation to surface patterns, tie them to affected accounts, and benchmark cost and quality before and after a fix. The buyers are engineering, product, and customer success teams, so B2B fits. Within B2B, Analytics is the closest subindustry, since the core product turns conversation data into insights and metrics. Engineering, Product and Design was the main alternative, but the product is insight-driven rather than a build tool or API.
Olympian Motors manufactures electric vehicles and sells them to consumers and fleets. That fits the Industrials domain, Automotive subindustry, which covers companies that sell vehicles.

Morf sells an integration and workflow automation platform to healthcare providers, syncing patient data across their tools and automating administrative tasks. That is software for managing clinical and operational workflows, which matches Healthcare IT.

Voltair sells autonomous drone fleets and drone-enabled inspection data, primarily to power utilities, which fits the Drones subindustry under Industrials. Energy was the other candidate, but the product is the drones themselves rather than power generation, grid equipment, or energy management.

Elimentary sells AI agents to private capital managers, starting with structured credit funds, to run their middle and back-office work, such as borrowing base calculations, loan tape processing, and NAV calculations. The buyers are financial firms and the product automates their financial operations, so the closest fit is Fintech. Of the Fintech subindustries, Asset Management fits best because the customers are fund managers and the work is fund operations. The other options, such as Banking and Exchange or Credit and Lending, describe holding assets or extending loans, which Elimentary does not do.

Tinfoil sells confidential-computing infrastructure, a developer API and a container platform that businesses use to run AI workloads with verifiable privacy. It also has a consumer chatbot, but the core product is a technical building block that other teams run on top of. That fits B2B better than Consumer. Within B2B, Security and Infrastructure are both plausible. The pitch centers on encryption, attestation and provable privacy, which is protecting data and systems, so I chose Security.

Future Fields manufactures recombinant proteins for biotech, life sciences, and pharma customers using a biomanufacturing platform. The closest fit is Drug Discovery and Delivery, since the customers are pharma and biotech companies and the product is a research and production platform rather than a finished therapeutic. Industrial Bio is the main alternative, but it covers non-therapeutic applications, which doesn't match this customer base.

RealPact sells transaction-automation software to real estate brokerages, so the closest fit is Real Estate and Construction. Within that domain, "Housing and Real Estate" covers transaction services for brokers and agents dealing with already-built properties, which matches a brokerage paperwork and closing workflow. "Construction" is about building structures, so it doesn't apply.

SubVysion sells underground utility mapping, built on autonomous rovers, to construction contractors. Its stated purpose is to help them avoid utility strikes and project delays, which places it in the Construction subindustry of Real Estate and Construction.

Hiration sells a SaaS product directly to individual job seekers. It helps them build resumes and cover letters, update their LinkedIn profiles, prepare for interviews and apply to jobs. That fits the Consumer domain, in the "Job and Career Services" subindustry.
JABU is a fintech company that provides B2B payments and digital wallets, which fits the Payments subindustry best.

Bobidi's Upswell platform is sold to local restaurants. It helps them acquire new guests and retain them as regulars through quiz-based loyalty campaigns built from their social media videos. That is a customer acquisition and retention tool, so Marketing fits best. Retail covers restaurant and merchant software, but the core function here is marketing and loyalty.

Axial sells GPU-accelerated geometry and physics simulation software to engineering teams. That is engineering software for manufacturers and industrial operators, which fits Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics ("engineering software ... to manufacturers"). B2B Engineering, Product and Design was the other candidate, but the manufacturing and computational engineering focus points to Industrials.

Plumter offers financial tools for importers and exporters, built on multi-currency and stablecoin infrastructure with AI-powered multilingual invoicing. Its core offering is moving money across borders to settle trade transactions, which fits Fintech Payments best. The invoicing and multi-currency account features support that payments focus rather than changing the category.

Azalea Robotics sells robotic systems that automate baggage handling to airports and airlines. The closest fit is Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics, which covers industrial automation and robots sold to operators to automate physical workflows. Supply Chain and Logistics (B2B) is a possible alternative, but it is defined around software and platforms for coordinating goods, and this company sells robots. Aviation and Space is aimed at spacecraft, aircraft engines and related infrastructure, so it fits less well.

FoodCourt runs virtual restaurants and dark stores and sells meals and convenience goods directly to individual consumers across Africa. That fits Consumer, and within it Food and Beverage, which covers edible products and restaurant or grocery delivery sold to individuals.

Toko is a consumer mobile app that teaches English speaking skills to individual learners. The closest fit is Consumer, Job and Career Services, which covers professional skill-building. The alternative is Other, which includes education, but Toko sells directly to consumers and its workplace-discussion practice leans toward career skills, so I chose Consumer.
Eclipse Foods makes plant-based dairy products, such as ice cream and cream cheese. It sells edible products, so the Consumer domain and its Food and Beverage subindustry fit best.

Humane Genomics engineers oncolytic viruses to treat cancer, with a first indication in pediatric liver cancer. Because the product is a therapeutic intended for regulatory approval and administration to patients, it fits Healthcare, Therapeutics.

Ranla sells an AI-driven lifecycle email marketing product to SaaS companies, covering segmentation, campaign planning, sending and reporting on conversions. That fits B2B Marketing, which covers software for acquiring, retaining and engaging customers through campaigns.

PokerClubHub sells a licensed online poker platform to individual players, who wager and play on it, and to club owners, who earn affiliate fees. Its core offering is real-money gaming and wagering, so Consumer / Gaming fits best.

Shor sells international payroll, employer-of-record (EOR) and contractor payment services to startups and businesses. The closest fit is B2B, since the product is payroll and global hiring compliance for companies. Within B2B, Human Resources is the better subindustry than Finance and Accounting, because core HR records, employment contracts and payroll fall under HR rather than bookkeeping, tax or accounts payable.

Beglaubigt.de sells company formation, notarization, and legal back-office services to founders and businesses. It also offers an incorporation API to fintech partners, and it is expanding into registered addresses, trade registrations, and bookkeeping. The core product is legal and corporate-formation workflows, so B2B Legal is the closest fit.

XGenomes is building a DNA sequencing platform made of new biochemistry, hardware and algorithms, sold first as a service and later as instruments and consumables. Sequencing tools of this kind detect and characterize genetic variants, so Diagnostics is the closest fit. The other candidates fit less well. Drug Discovery and Delivery is aimed at biotech and pharma research, and Medical Devices covers devices that interact with the body.

Vortexify sells an AI app builder to business operations teams for building internal apps (scheduling, forecasting, process optimization), which fits B2B Operations best. The alternatives, Productivity and Engineering, Product and Design, are more general or developer-facing, while this product targets operational workflows.

PostEra uses machine learning to speed up medicinal chemistry for small-molecule drug programs. It sells this through partnerships with biopharma companies such as Amgen and Pfizer. That fits the Drug Discovery and Delivery subindustry, which covers research platforms and computational tools sold to biotech and pharma companies. Its internal pipeline is secondary to the platform and partnership business.

Cortex AI sells robot and egocentric human data to frontier labs and robotics companies building embodied AI. Its closest fit is Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry. I considered B2B Infrastructure or Analytics, since it is a data provider. I chose Manufacturing and Robotics because the data and evaluation work is specific to robotics and physical workplaces.

Kite sells a screen-recording and video-editing tool to companies, mainly startups, for making product demo and launch videos. Its main use is promoting a product, so Marketing fits better than Productivity or Engineering, Product and Design.

HUBUC offers card issuing and payment processing infrastructure, which puts it in Fintech. Payments fits better than Banking and Exchange because the product is about processing card transactions rather than holding accounts or exchanging currency.

BotBuilt uses robotics to build houses, which is construction-focused. It sells to builders and contractors, with software and robotic systems that prefabricate framing, so Real Estate and Construction → Construction fits best, rather than Manufacturing and Robotics.

Talos sells monitoring devices and anomaly-detection software to utilities and power operators to maintain large transformers, which fits Industrials, Energy (grid infrastructure and monitoring of electricity assets).

ZeroSettle sells an SDK to app developers so they can bill customers directly instead of through the App Store. Its buyers are developer teams, and the product is a building block they integrate into their apps, which fits B2B Engineering, Product and Design. Payments was the main alternative, since the SDK handles billing and payouts. But the core offering is a developer-facing SDK, so I chose the developer-tools category.

StayQrious sells online group classes and coaching to kids in India, which is an education business sold to families. None of the Consumer subindustries cover education or tutoring (Job and Career Services is limited to employment and career skills), so it fits "Other", which includes education.

Segmed sells access to de-identified medical imaging and real-world data to life sciences companies and technology developers for research and AI model development. This is a data infrastructure product for healthcare organizations, so Healthcare IT fits better than Diagnostics or Drug Discovery and Delivery.

RendaloMaq rents heavy equipment to construction and mining customers in Latin America and runs it on its own software platform, ROS. Its customers are construction companies, so the best fit is Real Estate and Construction, subindustry Construction, rather than a B2B software category.

SpruceID builds digital identity infrastructure (decentralized identity, wallets, and verifiable credentials) sold to governments, enterprises, and blockchain ecosystems. That fits B2B, and the closest subindustry is Infrastructure, which covers identity and access management building blocks that other software runs on top of.

Remora builds modular carbon capture systems and sells the captured CO₂ to breweries and greenhouses. That is a carbon capture product for industrial and corporate customers, which fits the Climate subindustry of Industrials.

Dialogus sells AI voice agents to enterprises for customer support, sales, and collections, which is a contact center product. The closest B2B subindustry is Operations, which covers internal workflows and customer support. Sales and collections are part of the pitch, but customer support is the core use case, so Operations fits better than Sales.
Pyrls is a medical reference app sold to clinicians and healthcare organizations. It's software that supports prescribing, dispensing, and patient education workflows, so Healthcare IT fits best.

Covera sells AI agents to insurance brokers, so the main choice is between Fintech Insurance and a B2B category. The Insurance subindustry covers brokerage services and underwriting technology sold to consumers or businesses, which fits a tool built for brokers' servicing work like submission intake, quoting, and claims handling. I picked Fintech Insurance over B2B Operations because the product is specific to the insurance industry.

Spenny is a micro-investing app for individual consumers in India. It rounds up digital transactions and invests the spare change in a diversified portfolio, and it charges a fee on assets under management. That makes it a Fintech company, and Asset Management fits best because its core product is automated portfolio investing and its stated vision is to become a one-stop asset management solution. Consumer Finance was the main alternative, but investing is the central product.

Text Blaze is a text-expansion tool that lets teams save smart templates and insert them anywhere with keyboard shortcuts. It is general-purpose software that helps individuals and teams work faster across functions, so B2B Productivity fits best.

Spenmo sells spend management software to businesses. It covers bill payment, corporate cards, transfers, and expense claims, all aimed at streamlining accounts payable and bookkeeping. That fits B2B Finance and Accounting best. It does include payments features, but the core product is AP and finance-team software.
Auricle sells a physical neurostimulation implant to clinicians and patients that treats hearing loss, which fits Medical Devices.

Kenobi sells website personalization software to businesses, tailoring landing-page content to each visitor so more of them convert. That is a marketing function (acquiring and converting customers through site content), so Marketing fits better than Sales, Analytics or Engineering tools.

Nectar sells an AI energy management platform to facility and sustainability teams, along with a utility data API. That puts it in energy management and monitoring, which fits Industrials, Energy, better than B2B Analytics or Office Management.

Portão 3 is described as "Ramp for LATAM", a corporate spend and payments platform for companies. The one-liner stresses making payments, and Ramp-style products center on corporate cards and spend management, which are financial products. That points to Fintech, and Payments fits best because the company sells business payment infrastructure.

Theseus sells navigation software for drones operating where GPS is unavailable, which fits the Drones subindustry since it covers navigation systems for unmanned aerial vehicles. Defense is a plausible alternative given the anti-jamming focus, but the product is drone navigation, so Drones is the better match.

Vestris sells software to title companies, which are businesses that handle real estate closings. That puts it in Real Estate and Construction. Within that domain, the Housing and Real Estate subindustry covers transaction and inspection services for buying and selling already-built properties, and title processing for closings fits there. The Construction subindustry is for building structures, so it doesn't apply.

Edexia sells an AI grading assistant to teachers and educational institutions. The fund's domains treat education as "Other" (Education, government, nonprofits). It is not a general B2B tool, since its customers are schools and teachers rather than businesses.

Alba Orbital builds and launches satellites and sells earth observation imagery to government and commercial customers. That fits Industrials, in the Aviation and Space subindustry, which covers spacecraft, satellites, and related space data services sold to government agencies and commercial operators.

HippoBuild sells back-office automation and materials-sourcing software to small and medium construction companies. That fits Real Estate and Construction, and within it the Construction subindustry, which covers software sold to contractors to manage building work.

Velontra builds a hypersonic space plane that launches payloads into orbit and sells to government and commercial customers. That fits Industrials, in the Aviation and Space subindustry, which covers spacecraft and related space infrastructure for government agencies and commercial operators.

OnePatch sells an AI site reliability engineer to engineering teams. It handles on-call work by monitoring services, catching incidents, and driving them to resolution. That is infrastructure and operations tooling for developers, so B2B fits. Of the B2B subindustries, Infrastructure is the closest match because the product runs alongside production systems and manages their reliability. Operations is a plausible alternative, but Infrastructure fits better for an SRE and observability product.

Playgent sells sandbox infrastructure to engineering teams building AI agents. Its MCP-based environments reproduce production failures and export OTel traces. That is a technical building block that other software runs on top of, so I classed it under B2B Infrastructure. Engineering, Product and Design was the closest alternative, but it fits tools for shipping products less well than infrastructure for running and testing agents.

GRU Space builds hardware that makes bricks from lunar regolith and inflatable habitats, and plans to land on the Moon in 2027. It sells spacecraft-delivered infrastructure for operations beyond Earth, which fits Aviation and Space better than Construction or Travel, since the hotel is a long-term goal rather than the current product.

Probably Genetic sells a data platform to drug developers and patient advocacy groups. It finds undiagnosed patients, analyzes their disease state, and enables communication with them. The buyers are pharma and biotech companies, so the best fit is a platform serving drug developers rather than a consumer health product. The closest healthcare subindustries are Healthcare IT and Drug Discovery and Delivery. Healthcare IT is aimed at providers and payers, while Drug Discovery and Delivery covers research platforms and tools sold to biotech and pharma. The company's patient identification and recruitment for clinical trials and treatments for drug developers fits Drug Discovery and Delivery best.

Alloovium sells document intelligence software to construction companies. It reads project contracts, specs, drawings, and compliance records, so it belongs in Real Estate and Construction, under the Construction subindustry.

Gridware sells smart sensors to utility companies to monitor the electrical grid and detect, locate, and prevent outages and wildfires. This fits Industrials, in the Energy subindustry, which covers grid infrastructure, metering, and energy management products sold to utilities.

JetPack Aviation develops optionally piloted VTOL aircraft (flying motorcycles) for heavy lift and cargo delivery. Among the available subindustries, "Aviation and Space" covers aircraft sold to commercial operators and government agencies, which fits best. Automotive excludes aerial vehicles, and Drones covers unmanned aerial vehicles specifically.

Ageospatial sells geospatial AI to insurance carriers and MGAs. It helps them assess and price property risk for underwriting, claims and pricing. That points to Fintech, and within Fintech the Insurance subindustry covers underwriting and risk-assessment technology sold to insurers.

Alice.tech sells AI-driven exam prep directly to college students. That is education, which the fund's definitions place under "Other" (education, government, nonprofits). The Consumer "Job and Career Services" subindustry covers employment and career-skill tools, not academic exam prep, so it doesn't fit.

Daybreak delivers teletherapy and psychiatry through clinicians to youth and partners with schools and pediatric groups. That is a care delivery service performed by people rather than a software or hardware product, so it fits Healthcare Services.

The company sells an HR-focused platform that starts with HR data integrations and expands into agentic HR analysts for People Ops teams. It is sold to businesses and built around HR, so B2B / Human Resources is the closest fit. Analytics is a possible alternative, but the product is aimed squarely at HR functions.

Proof of Human sells an API to platforms that detects bots and verifies users are human. This is a developer-facing building block for identity verification. It could also be read as Security, but the fund's definition of "Engineering, Product and Design" explicitly names identity verification building blocks sold as APIs, so I'm classifying it there.

Guardian Bio develops a cell-based cancer therapy. It takes stem cells from patients, turns them into dendritic cells trained against the patient's own tumor, and re-infuses them. That is a therapeutic product meant for regulatory approval, so Healthcare, Therapeutics is the best fit.

ACX sells biological crop-protection products, an alternative to chemical pesticides, to growers. That fits Industrials, in the Agriculture subindustry, which covers crop and farm products sold to growers and agribusinesses, including pesticide discovery.

Warpfy sells home and kitchen products directly to consumers (D2C and marketplaces), with a smaller B2B wholesale channel. Its core is a consumer home lifestyle brand, so Consumer / Home and Personal fits best.

Notabene sells compliance software (the crypto "Travel Rule" and counterparty due diligence) to crypto businesses. The Fintech subindustry definitions place "core banking and compliance software to... financial institutions" and crypto trading infrastructure under Banking and Exchange. Payments also covers fraud prevention and money transfer infrastructure, but Notabene's focus is regulatory compliance for crypto transactions, which fits Banking and Exchange better.

Assembly is an HOA management company that serves homeowner associations, boards and residents, using software to run community operations. That puts it in property and community management, which falls under Housing and Real Estate: it sells services to landlords, boards and homeowners to manage already-built residential properties.

Impossible Metals builds underwater robotic vehicles to selectively harvest polymetallic nodules, which contain battery metals, from the seabed. Its customers would be battery and EV supply chains buying the metals, and the business is essentially mining.

The closest fit among the available categories is Industrials. Within it, Manufacturing and Robotics would cover the robotics hardware, but Climate and Energy don't describe a mining company. Automotive is also a poor fit because it covers ground vehicles. I chose Manufacturing and Robotics because the core product is autonomous robotic vehicles for an industrial operation.

Ancana sells fractional ownership of vacation homes to individual buyers, which fits best as a marketplace for buying and managing already-built residential property. That points to Real Estate and Construction, in the Housing and Real Estate subindustry. The other candidates fit less well: Travel, Leisure and Tourism covers trip booking and stays rather than ownership, and Fintech's Asset Management covers investment tools rather than a real share of a home with usage rights.

Swadesh sells a free checking account, credit card, SIM card and remittances directly to immigrants. That makes it a consumer-facing neobank. Within Fintech, "Consumer Finance" fits better than "Banking and Exchange", because it serves an underserved demographic and covers their everyday financial lives (banking, credit building, communication, remittance, insurance, housing).

Taiga sells AI software to doctors' offices that handles medical coding, claim checking, submission to insurers, and denial management. That is software for managing a provider's administrative and financial workflows, so it fits Healthcare IT.

HyLight sells unmanned airships, a cross between a drone and an airship, along with inspection services, to operators of pipelines, power lines and railways. The Drones subindustry covers unmanned aerial vehicles and drone-enabled inspection services for commercial customers, which is the closest match.

Goldbridge sells an AI-powered banking and financial management platform to real estate owners, with business accounts, yield on idle reserves, and expense management, much like Ramp does for businesses generally. Its core product is deposit accounts and spend management for businesses, so I've placed it in Fintech under Banking and Exchange rather than under Real Estate, where the buyers sit but the product is financial.

Sirdab sells a cloud warehousing and logistics platform to businesses. It gives them on-demand warehouse space plus tools to manage, optimize and distribute inventory, which fits B2B Supply Chain and Logistics.

MICSI sells AI software to imaging centers that improves MRI resolution and cuts scan times. It is software for healthcare providers' clinical and operational workflows, and it is not a diagnostic test or a hardware device. That makes Healthcare IT the closest fit, though Diagnostics is a plausible alternative since the software is image-analysis tooling.

Ascenix sells software to skilled nursing facilities. It analyzes EHR data to automate reporting, recover missed reimbursement, and flag compliance gaps and clinical risks. This is software for healthcare providers that manages clinical, financial, and operational workflows, so Healthcare IT fits best.

Albiware sells an all-in-one software platform to damage repair contractors, covering project management, field documentation, scheduling, CRM and more. Its customers are construction and restoration contractors, so Real Estate and Construction → Construction is the closest fit, rather than a general B2B category.
Juicy Marbles sells plant-based steaks, which are edible products sold to individual consumers, so it fits Consumer, Food and Beverage.

Illuminant Surgical sells a physical projection system, Skylight™, to clinicians. It shows anatomical images directly on the patient to guide interventions, which makes it hardware that directly supports medical procedures, so Medical Devices fits best.

Pools sells a memberships platform to event organizers, such as art and music communities. These are businesses that use it to upsell ticket buyers into memberships and manage the benefits. Its customers are organizers rather than consumers, so it fits B2B, and the closest subindustry is Marketing, since the product retains and engages customers through membership upsells at ticket checkout.

Betterhalf sells a matchmaking and wedding app directly to individual consumers, so it falls under Consumer. Within Consumer, Social fits best, since the core offering is matchmaking and connecting people, which the Social definition explicitly covers.

Stellon Labs sells AI models that developers embed in devices and applications. Their first release, KittenTTS, is an open-source text-to-speech model. That puts the buyer in the developer and product-team category, so I'm classifying it under B2B, Engineering, Product and Design.

IronLedger sells accounts payable automation, corporate cards, and invoice processing to property managers, developers, and contractors. The product is accounting software for businesses, and real estate is only the vertical it serves. That makes B2B Finance and Accounting a better fit than Real Estate and Construction, which is aimed at property marketplaces and construction project tools.

Lantern AI sells software to businesses that runs the full hiring process: sourcing, inbound applications, interviews, assessments, candidate communication, and offers. That fits B2B, Recruiting and Talent, which covers tools for sourcing, screening, and hiring candidates, rather than broader HR platforms for managing employees after they are hired.

Adravision sells AI software to dental clinics and dental insurers. It covers diagnostics, documentation, patient education and claims processing. That is software for healthcare providers and payers that manages clinical and administrative workflows, so Healthcare IT fits best. Diagnostics is the closest alternative, but the claims-processing and documentation work points to Healthcare IT.

Sivo sells lending infrastructure: an API and risk protocol plus debt capital that lets fintechs, neobanks, and gig platforms lend to their own users. That fits Fintech, and within it Credit and Lending, whose definition includes lending infrastructure and automation for institutions seeking to extend capital.

TRM Labs sells blockchain analytics and an AI investigations platform to government agencies, law enforcement, and financial institutions for crime fighting, fraud, and compliance. The closest fit is the Security subindustry under B2B, since it protects systems and data through threat detection and investigation. Analytics and Fintech compliance are plausible alternatives, but the crime-fighting focus makes Security the best match.

Topline Pro sells software to home service businesses (the professionals, not homeowners), covering website creation, SEO, local listings, social media, and online payments. Its main purpose is helping those businesses be discovered and booked by customers, which is customer acquisition and engagement. That fits B2B Marketing best.

CreativeMode sells an AI tool that lets individual Minecraft players create and share mods and play them with friends. Its customers are consumers, and the core product is a game-adjacent creation and play experience, so Consumer / Gaming fits best.

Sidekick sells an AI agent to custom manufacturers and shop floors. It reads live machine data, routes work orders, places purchase orders, and answers workers' questions from the shop's own documents. The closest fit is Industrials, in the Manufacturing and Robotics subindustry, which covers automation and software sold to manufacturers and industrial operators. The B2B Operations category was the alternative, but the product is built specifically for factory floor operations, so the manufacturing category is the better match.

Lyon sells foundation models to banks, insurers, and fintechs, trained on their own transaction data to predict credit, fraud, collections, churn, and lifetime value. Its customers are financial institutions, so Fintech is the right domain. Of the Fintech subindustries, Credit and Lending fits best: credit and fraud prediction are the main use cases, and the first deployment under way is for credit. Insurance and Payments are weaker fits, since Lyon sells modeling technology rather than policies or transaction processing.

Usul sells an AI platform to companies so they can find and win government contracts. That is a software tool for sales and business development, so I'm placing it in B2B Sales rather than Defense, since it does not sell defense technology itself.

DreamWorld is a consumer game and user-generated-content platform sold directly to players, so Gaming fits better than Virtual and Augmented Reality, since the value is gameplay and building rather than immersive spatial simulation.

Magic Hour serves two audiences. Creators and teams use it in the browser to generate and edit media, and developers integrate the same capabilities through a REST API, SDKs, and an MCP server.

The Consumer media options (Content, VR/AR) don't fit well, since the product is a creation tool rather than consumable content or immersive tech. The best fit is B2B, in the subindustry for developer- and product-team-facing tools such as APIs and SDKs. The alternative is B2B Productivity, but the API, SDK, and MCP offering points to Engineering, Product and Design.

Relevium Medical is developing an injectable gel drug for knee osteoarthritis. It has completed preclinical testing and is aiming for regulatory approval, which fits Therapeutics (a drug intended to treat disease) better than Medical Devices or Drug Discovery and Delivery.

SaveIN's main product is financing: it splits medical bills into monthly instalments, which is a lending product. It also helps people discover nearby healthcare practices, but the core offering is credit for paying for care, so Fintech fits better than Healthcare. Within Fintech, Credit and Lending fits better than Consumer Finance, because it provides the credit itself.
Cityfurnish rents furniture and appliances to individual renters in India, so it sells a home-related product directly to consumers. The closest fit is Consumer, Home and Personal.

Mathos is an AI math solver and personalized learning tool for students and teachers, which is education. The fund's domains have no education category, and "Other" explicitly covers education, so that is the best fit.

Tandem is an office leasing broker that helps tenant companies find and lease office space. That fits the Real Estate and Construction domain, and within it, Housing and Real Estate, which covers search tools and transaction services for brokers, landlords and tenants dealing with already-built commercial properties.

Structured AI sells AI-powered drawing review (QA/QC) software to architects and engineers, helping them catch errors in construction drawing sets before they go out. Its customers are firms that design and plan buildings, and the product is used to plan and check the physical construction of structures, so it fits Real Estate and Construction, in the Construction subindustry.

Oasive sells AI-driven research and analytics to bond investors, such as portfolio managers, traders and analysts. That makes it a Fintech company. Within Fintech, the closest fit is Asset Management, since it serves investment decision-making for funds and institutions.

Kater.ai sells enterprise analytics software that turns a business question into generated analysis code and insights. That matches the B2B Analytics subindustry, which covers software that models business data and produces insights for decision-makers.

Pickle sells directly to individual consumers: a personal AI memory layer, a web chat app, and AI-powered AR glasses (Pickle 1). The closest fit is Consumer, since the product is aimed at individuals rather than businesses.

For the subindustry, the main candidates are Consumer Electronics and Virtual and Augmented Reality. Virtual and Augmented Reality covers immersive 3D and AR experiences, but Pickle's glasses mainly capture personal context for an AI memory system rather than deliver immersive content. Their core value is a personal AI and memory operating system, with the glasses as a hardware device for it. Consumer Electronics, which covers consumer hardware like wearables, is therefore the better fit.

Djamo is a consumer-facing challenger bank, so it belongs in Fintech. Of the Fintech subindustries, Banking and Exchange fits best because it sells deposit accounts and banking services. Consumer Finance is the closest alternative, but Djamo's core product is the bank account itself rather than broader financial planning.

HeartByte's product, Storio, is a platform where creators write interactive fiction with generative AI and readers consume it. Its core offering is produced fiction content for individual consumers. That fits Consumer, Content better than Social, where the core value would be interpersonal connection rather than reading stories.

TagMango sells a SaaS tool to creators, who use it to build paid communities and monetise their audiences. Its customers are businesses (creators), so B2B is the best-fit domain. The closest subindustry is Marketing, which covers engaging and retaining customers and audiences. Productivity is too generic, and Sales is aimed at managing sales pipelines.

Blixo sells accounts receivable automation (invoicing, collections, cash application, and subscription billing) to businesses. That fits B2B, Finance and Accounting, which covers accounts payable/receivable software.

Coderhouse sells live online tech courses directly to individual learners so they can build skills they can use on the job. That matches the Consumer domain's "Job and Career Services" subindustry, which covers selling tools, marketplaces, or content to individuals for building professional skills and advancing their careers. The education angle could point to "Other", but that category is a fallback for companies the other domains don't describe, and this one fits Job and Career Services directly.

Axel Travel is an AI agent that finds travel deals, offers negotiated rates, and refunds money if prices drop after booking. That is a consumer-facing travel booking and savings service, so it fits Travel, Leisure and Tourism.

Ditto Bio is developing its own autoimmune therapies by using AI to find and engineer parasite-derived proteins. That makes it a drug developer rather than a seller of research tools or platforms to other biotech companies, so Therapeutics fits better than Drug Discovery and Delivery.

Moonvalley builds generative video and image foundation models and a creative studio for making content with them. The closest fit is Consumer, since its core offering is tools for creating immersive visual content. Among the Consumer subindustries, Content is the nearest match, because the product is generated video and image media. Virtual and Augmented Reality doesn't fit, as the company isn't focused on spatial or 3D immersion.

trii is an investing platform for retail investors in Latin America. That fits Fintech, and within it Asset Management, which covers platforms for individual investors to invest and manage their assets.

Roforco is a game studio that makes original games on Roblox and sells them directly to individual players, so Consumer and then Gaming is the closest fit. Virtual and Augmented Reality doesn't apply because the games are traditional gameplay rather than immersive 3D/spatial simulation.

Datafold sells AI-driven tools to data engineering teams for testing, code review, and data platform migrations. Of the available categories, "Engineering, Product and Design" fits best because its customers are developers and technical teams building data products. "Infrastructure" and "Analytics" are close alternatives, but Datafold doesn't provide the underlying systems or dashboards and metrics, so I ruled them out.

AlgoUniversity sells job-focused tech training to individual college students and gets paid through income-sharing agreements once they land jobs. Of the available options, "Job and Career Services" fits best, since it covers platforms that build professional skills and help people advance their careers. "Other" (education) was the alternative, but the job-placement focus points to Job and Career Services.

StartPlaying.Games is a marketplace that connects individual players with game masters who host tabletop games like D&D, so it sells to consumers and fits the Gaming subindustry. Its core offering is access to gameplay sessions rather than a social network or produced content.

Poka Labs sells an AI platform to sales reps at chemical manufacturers to price, quote, and respond to customer requests. The product is sales software for businesses, so B2B Sales is the best fit. Industrials/Manufacturing was the other candidate, but that subindustry covers automation and engineering tools for producing goods, not tools for selling them.
ANORIA sells a wearable device directly to individual consumers, so I classified it as Consumer Electronics rather than Consumer Health and Wellness, since the product is the hardware itself.

Eazipay's core product is payroll and payment automation software sold to businesses. It handles salary payments, tax deductions, and compliance, with a Payroll API for fintechs and platforms. Early wage access and financial wellness tools for workers are secondary features. The closest fits are Fintech (Payments) and B2B (Human Resources or Finance and Accounting).

Payroll is the main business, and its buyers are businesses. The fund's definitions place payroll tools under "Human Resources" or "Finance and Accounting", and the Finance and Accounting definition explicitly contrasts itself with "HR-focused payroll tools". Eazipay is also payment automation infrastructure, and its API and early wage access are fintech-style offerings, so Fintech Payments is a strong alternative.

I chose Fintech (Payments). Its offering centers on automating salary disbursements through an API that fintechs and platforms embed, which is payment infrastructure. Early wage access adds to the fintech character.

Workpay sells payroll software, Employer of Record services, compliance, and HR tools to companies. Its core offering is payroll and workforce management for businesses, which fits B2B Human Resources, since the one-liner and description centre on payroll, benefits, and HR records rather than on recruiting.

Simplify's main product, Copilot, is sold directly to individual job seekers to help them find and apply to jobs. That makes Consumer / Job and Career Services the best fit. The company is also expanding toward recruiters, but the core business today is serving candidates.
Beyond Aero builds hydrogen-electric business aircraft, which fits Aviation and Space (aircraft and related infrastructure sold to commercial operators) better than Climate or Energy.

Locale sells prepared organic, high-protein meals directly to individual consumers, which fits the Consumer domain's Food and Beverage subindustry (edible products and meal delivery for personal consumption).

Shasta Health sells AI software to healthcare provider organizations to automate front-office and administrative workflows (calls, insurance verification, prior authorizations), which fits Healthcare IT.

GiveAway is a consumer marketplace where individuals list used household items and other users bid on them with virtual coins. It sells to individual consumers and is built around decluttering the home and finding secondhand goods cheaply. The closest fit is Consumer, Home and Personal, since it centers on personal and household needs rather than apparel, electronics, or social networking.

Molagri develops biopesticides for agriculture, which are sold to growers and agribusinesses. That fits Industrials, Agriculture, whose definition explicitly includes pesticide discovery. The climate angle (lower emissions) is secondary to the core product.
Ivy Homes is an iBuyer: it buys already-built homes directly from sellers and resells them, so it fits Real Estate and Construction under Housing and Real Estate.

SpotPay is a stablecoin-based neobank that gives individual users one global account to receive money, spend by card and save. Banking and Exchange fits best because it centres on account-holding and currency exchange rather than transaction processing alone.

Consumer Finance is a possible alternative, but the core product is the account itself.
Fresco sells AI takeoff and estimating software to general contractors and Division 8 subcontractors, which fits the Construction subindustry of Real Estate and Construction.
Red Barn Robotics sells an autonomous weeding robot to farmers, so Agriculture fits better than Manufacturing and Robotics, which excludes agriculture-specific applications.

Deskimo sells on-demand workspace access to companies for their hybrid workforces, as an extension of the corporate office. The customer is the business, and the product is about managing where employees physically work. That fits B2B Office Management, which covers workspace and facilities management.

Boat sells cloud VMs (sandboxes) that developers and teams run AI agents on. That is compute infrastructure used by engineering teams, so B2B Infrastructure fits better than Engineering, Product and Design.

Farmtheory sells vegetables and produce to restaurants, connecting farms with business buyers. That makes it a B2B supply chain and distribution business rather than a consumer food product. The "Supply Chain and Logistics" subindustry in B2B covers wholesale distribution and logistics coordination of physical goods between suppliers and buyers, which fits best. Industrials/Agriculture is a possible alternative, but the core offering is the farm-to-restaurant delivery and value chain.

Curacel sells AI software to insurers, third-party administrators and healthcare providers to automate claims processing and detect fraud. That fits Fintech Insurance (underwriting and risk-assessment technology for insurers) slightly better than Healthcare IT. The claims and fraud-detection workflows are core insurance operations, and insurers are its primary customers.

LFcarry sells game boosting, carry and coaching services to individual gamers through a marketplace, which fits Consumer / Gaming. Gamers are the buyers, and the product is game-adjacent entertainment and services.

Milliray builds radar systems to detect and track small drones, sold to defense, airport, and critical infrastructure customers. That is a surveillance and countermeasure product for security and military buyers, so Defense fits better than Drones, which covers companies that sell or operate drones themselves.

BBy sells a device and process to hospitals and NICUs that turns breast milk into a shelf-stable powder, saving nursing time and reducing milk waste. The closest fit is Healthcare, since the buyer is a hospital and the product is a physical device used in clinical care. Within Healthcare, Medical Devices is the best match, though it does not directly monitor, diagnose, or treat a condition through contact with the body. The alternatives fit worse: Healthcare Services is delivered by people, not hardware, and Consumer Health and Wellness targets individual consumers, not hospitals.

Oda is an AI home design agent. Homebuyers and renters use it to find their design preferences and shop for furniture and décor. It reaches them through real estate platform partners, who embed it on their sites. The end user is an individual consumer managing their home, which fits Consumer / Home and Personal. The alternative, Real Estate / Housing and Real Estate, covers tools for finding, marketing, buying or selling properties. Oda's core product is home design and furnishing discovery, not property transactions.

AccioJob trains individual graduates in tech skills and places them in jobs. That is a service sold to individual consumers to build skills and advance their careers, so it fits Consumer, Job and Career Services. The hiring-partner side exists, but the core offering is the skilling and placement of candidates.

Eze sells IT asset management, procurement, and buyback software to businesses. Of the B2B subindustries, Operations fits best because its definition covers internal workflows and IT service management that don't fit cleanly into finance, HR, sales, or marketing. Supply Chain and Logistics was a possible alternative because of the procurement side, but the core product is tracking and managing a company's own IT assets.

Tegore is an AI math tutor for K-12 students, built around school curriculum and aimed at a consumer product described as a "Duolingo for Math". Its customers are students and schools, so it falls under education, which the fund files under Other. None of the consumer subindustries (such as Job and Career Services) cover K-12 education.
Kosh sells loans directly to blue-collar workers in India, so it fits Fintech and, within that, Credit and Lending.

Flockjay sells sales enablement software (learning, content, and coaching) to businesses' sales teams. That fits the B2B domain, and Sales is the closest subindustry because the product is built for sales teams.
Vena Vitals sells a wearable sticker that continuously monitors blood pressure, a physical device that interacts with the body to monitor a medical condition. That fits Medical Devices.

Seeing Systems builds autonomous strike drones for military customers (UK Royal Marines and NATO forces). Two subindustries fit: Defence, which covers weapons systems sold to military customers for combat, and Drones, which covers unmanned aerial vehicles. The product is a strike drone designed for combat and sold to militaries, so Defense is the better match.

Rise Reforming converts waste biogas into chemicals such as dimethyl ether and methanol. Its main value is in producing low-carbon, locally sourced chemicals from waste gas, so Climate is a better fit than Energy or Manufacturing and Robotics. The customers are industrial: wastewater plants, chemical buyers and fuel additive buyers.

Trusty is a marketplace that connects buyers, homeowners, and real estate agents to find and transact on homes, including ones not listed for sale. That fits Housing and Real Estate, which covers marketplaces and search tools for buying and selling already-built properties.
Handoff sells AI estimating and business-operations software to remodelers and contractors, which fits Real Estate and Construction, and within it the Construction subindustry.
Omoi is a subscription service that sells manga, a form of produced media, directly to individual readers, which fits the Consumer domain's Content subindustry.

Powder sells to wealth advisors and firms, and its product automates their sales proposals, so it is software for the sales function and fits B2B Sales better than Fintech Asset Management. The document parsing, meeting notes and portfolio analysis all serve to win new clients, not to manage assets directly.

Chari's core offering is a B2B ordering and delivery marketplace that lets small retailers buy consumer goods from suppliers, with microloans as an added service. This is wholesale distribution of physical goods, so Supply Chain and Logistics fits better than Retail (storefront software) or Credit and Lending.

Andi is a search engine sold directly to individual consumers. It is ad-free and privacy-focused, and it gives people answers and summaries to read instead of links. Of the Consumer subindustries, Content fits best, since the offering is informational content consumed by the user. Social doesn't apply because the core value isn't connecting with other people.

TransAstra sells spacecraft propulsion, orbital transfer vehicles and space-domain-awareness telescope data to government agencies such as the Space Force and to commercial space operators. That matches the Aviation and Space subindustry, which covers spacecraft, space infrastructure and space data services sold to government and commercial operators.

Charm is a consumer-facing payments app for sending money to anyone, and it pays interest on balances. Its core offering is moving money between people, which fits Payments best. The interest on balances is a secondary feature.

Okani sells a low-cost wellness membership directly to consumers in Mexico. It delivers digital primary care through chat and an app, and coordinates secondary care with physicians, labs, pharmacies and clinics. That is care delivery and coordination by people, not software sold to providers, so Healthcare Services fits best. Consumer Health and Wellness was the main alternative, but the care is clinical rather than self-directed wellness.

Bamboo is an online brokerage that gives individual investors and their asset managers direct access to US and global securities, so it fits Fintech. Within Fintech, Asset Management fits better than Banking and Exchange because the product is aimed at investing and portfolio management, including a tool for managing multiple portfolios.

Inspectify is a home inspection platform. It sells inspection services and tools to homebuyers, agents and inspectors, which fits the Housing and Real Estate subindustry, defined as "transaction and inspection services to homebuyers, renters, brokers, landlords, and agents" for already-built properties.

FlowManual sells AI estimating, bidding, and purchasing software to general and MEP construction contractors, which fits Real Estate and Construction. Within that domain, Construction is the better match than Housing and Real Estate, because its customers are contractors planning and managing the physical building of structures.

Algen uses CRISPR and machine learning to find first-in-class drugs for cancer and inflammation. The description frames it as a drug discovery company: it finds treatments rather than selling a finished therapeutic. Algen is known for providing a CRISPR-based discovery platform and partnering with pharma, which fits Drug Discovery and Delivery, though its aim of finding its own drugs could also fit Therapeutics. I chose Drug Discovery and Delivery because the emphasis is on the platform for identifying drug candidates.

Kiwi Biosciences develops enzymes that break down dietary triggers for people with IBS. It most likely sells these as consumer supplements that individuals take with meals to manage their digestive health. That fits Consumer Health and Wellness better than Therapeutics, which is for drugs developed for regulatory approval to treat disease.

Modulari-T engineers immune cells with synthetic genes so they can recognize and kill cancer cells. The product is cell and gene therapy intended to treat disease, which fits Therapeutics best. It is not a research tool sold to drug developers, and it is not a delivery technology.
Vouch sells business insurance policies and brokerage to startups and growth-stage companies, which places it in Fintech under Insurance.

Origami Therapeutics is developing oral small-molecule protein degraders to treat Huntington's disease and other neurodegenerative conditions. Because it is building a drug candidate for regulatory approval rather than selling a research platform to other companies, Therapeutics fits better than Drug Discovery and Delivery.

ProvenMetal makes circuit boards and automates the manufacturing steps, so the Industrials domain fits better than B2B software. Within it, Manufacturing and Robotics is the closest subindustry, since the company sells factory automation and manufactured goods to industrial customers.

Exin Therapeutics is developing therapeutics for neurological disorders, using AI models and in-house mouse studies to find compounds that modify neural activity. The AI and mouse screening are tools for discovering the drugs, and the company is building its own drug candidates rather than selling a platform to biotech and pharma customers. That fits Therapeutics better than Drug Discovery and Delivery.

Cinapse sells production scheduling software to filmmakers and production teams, which is a business workflow tool. Of the B2B subindustries, Operations fits best, since it covers internal workflows and project and process operations that don't fit finance, HR, sales, or marketing. Productivity is a close second, but the product is built for one specific function (film and TV production scheduling) rather than general-purpose work.

Units is an education company that lets students finish high school in one year with accredited diploma credits. None of the sector domains (B2B, Consumer, Fintech, Healthcare, Industrials, Real Estate) fit, since education falls under "Other".

Heyfood is a food delivery service that sells directly to individual consumers (urban Millennials and Gen Z professionals), which fits the Consumer domain's Food and Beverage subindustry, defined as including grocery and restaurant delivery services.

Cuanto sells software to merchants (storefront, payments, fulfillment) so they can sell online. That matches the B2B Retail subindustry: software for merchants to manage storefronts and consumer-facing commerce operations.

Instalab sells preventative health tests directly to individual consumers (founders, executives, athletes) for self-directed health monitoring, which fits Consumer Health and Wellness best. Diagnostics was the other candidate, but that category is aimed at clinicians, labs, and patients detecting disease, while Instalab's offering is a consumer-facing preventative service.
Cyclon sells a phone, which is a physical hardware device for individual consumers. That puts it in Consumer Electronics.

Strand AI sells foundation models to pharmaceutical companies that predict missing patient biology data, which they use to select better patients for drug trials and speed up launch timelines. That is a research and computational tool for biotech and pharma customers, not a finished therapeutic, so Drug Discovery and Delivery is the closest fit.

Liv Labs sells a physical pelvic floor resistance device directly to women for fitness and wellness. It is not a clinical diagnostic or a treatment sold through providers, so Consumer Health and Wellness fits better than Medical Devices.

Counter-drone systems sold to the Department of War (Defense) are weapons and countermeasure technologies for military customers, which fits the Defense subindustry better than Drones, since the company stops drones rather than selling them.

Hazel sells procurement software to government agencies. The fund's "Other" domain covers government and similar customers, but the product is business-process software for buyers. The closest B2B fit is Operations, which covers internal workflows that don't fit finance, HR, sales, or marketing. I'm choosing B2B Operations over "Other", because the software itself is a workflow tool and the government customer is secondary.

CoArena is a crowdsourced benchmark and evaluation data platform for computer-use AI models. Its main customers are AI labs and developers who want to test and improve their agents. That fits B2B Analytics (benchmarks and evaluation metrics) better than Engineering, Product and Design, which is for developer building blocks like APIs and SDKs.
Fazeshift sells software to businesses that automates accounts receivable, which falls under B2B Finance and Accounting (bookkeeping, accounts payable/receivable).

Ramen VR builds XR and AI tools for game developers, and it is also making its own games (it previously shipped Zenith: The Last City). The stated focus is tools that empower creators of online games and virtual worlds. That makes the primary customer developers, which points to B2B Engineering, Product and Design rather than a consumer gaming or VR/AR category.

However, it also builds its own game, and its history is as a VR game studio. The consumer VR/Gaming categories cover companies that sell games or immersive experiences directly to consumers. The description leads with "transforming game development with advanced XR + AI tools", so I'm going with the developer-tools framing.

Webiny sells an open-source framework to developers for building serverless applications, which makes it a developer-facing tool. The closest fit among the B2B subindustries is Engineering, Product and Design. Infrastructure was the other candidate, but Webiny is a framework developers build apps with, not the compute or identity layer that software runs on.

Moving Atoms sells a world-model simulator to robot labs, which use it to train robots on GPUs rather than on manually collected data. The customers are robotics developers, so Industrials fits better than Consumer VR/AR despite the "Virtual Reality" tagline. Within Industrials, Manufacturing and Robotics is the closest subindustry, since it covers robots and engineering software used to automate physical workflows.

Pluto.markets is a retail investing app aimed at underserved non-Euro European consumers. The closest fit is Fintech, but the subindustry is a judgment call between Asset Management, Banking and Exchange, and Consumer Finance. I chose Asset Management because the product is a platform for individual investors to buy and manage stock market investments.

Roofr sells software to roofing contractors for aerial measurements and proposals. Its customers are construction companies that plan and bid physical building work, so Real Estate and Construction fits, and within that the Construction subindustry is the match.

Vexo is a wearable bracelet sold to individual consumers, so Consumer Electronics fits best. Its core product is a physical gadget with a microphone and health sensors. The AI memory and task features run on that hardware, and the bracelet is not a VR/AR device.

Flai sells AI voice assistants to car dealerships. These answer inbound calls around the clock, book test drives and service appointments, and run outbound recall campaigns. The buyer is a business, and the product is aimed at lead capture and customer engagement, which points to B2B.

Within B2B, Sales fits best. The product captures and converts leads and books appointments, which is a revenue-driving function. Marketing (campaigns, lead generation) and Operations (customer support) were the other candidates, but the focus on never missing a sales opportunity makes Sales the closest match.

Illume sells directly to individual consumers, who use it for self-directed health and longevity insight rather than clinical diagnosis or treatment by a provider. That fits Healthcare, Consumer Health and Wellness.

Pibit.ai sells underwriting automation software to insurance carriers and MGAs, which fits the Fintech Insurance subindustry. That subindustry explicitly covers underwriting and risk-assessment technology sold to insurance businesses.

The company matches job seekers with roles at deep technology startups and fills skill gaps, so the question is whether it sells to individuals or to businesses. The one-liner frames it from the job seeker's side, but the description says it solves the startups' difficulty in filling specialized roles. That makes startups the paying customers, and the business is recruiting and talent placement for them.

T3 Chat's main product is an AI chat app that individuals use to talk to multiple AI models, and it is sold as a general-purpose productivity tool. The company's other products, such as UploadThing for developers, are secondary. I classified it as B2B Productivity, since it sells general-purpose software that helps people work faster across functions.

Vista Power sells solar and battery storage systems, with financing, installation and management, to commercial, industrial and multifamily property owners. That is power generation and energy management for business customers, which fits Industrials, Energy.

Orange Health Labs sells lab diagnostic testing to consumers, with at-home sample collection and fast reports. That fits Healthcare, and Diagnostics is the closest subindustry because the company sells tests that detect and measure disease states.

Plura is a consumer social and dating app. It sells community and connection to individual users, which fits the Consumer domain's Social subindustry, defined as platforms for connecting with other people, including matchmaking.

Perceptive sells a robotic system with imaging and AI to dentists, which perform surgery directly on the patient's body. That fits Healthcare, and the closest subindustry is Medical Devices, which covers physical hardware that diagnoses or treats a condition through interaction with the body. Healthcare IT and Diagnostics are weaker fits because the core product is the surgical robot rather than software or a test.

Tendo is a dropshipping platform that connects individual sellers to local wholesalers. It handles sourcing, delivery and payment, which fits the Supply Chain and Logistics definition: software for wholesale distribution between suppliers and buyers. The sellers are individuals reselling through social commerce, but the core product is the wholesale-to-reseller link, so B2B fits better than Consumer.
Careerist sells training and job-application automation directly to individual job seekers to help them move into tech careers, which fits Consumer, Job and Career Services.
